Industry News: If Your Google Pixel's Camera Is Suddenly Broken, Here's the Fix

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (421 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that updates are generally good for your devices.
  • Sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel customers are discovering this week.
  • Here's the situation: Following the November patch, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome revision, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel customers are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November update apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Here's the situation: Following the November patch, some users are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the issue is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

Industry observers note that to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel users are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some users are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

What does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

If your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November upgrade, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the issue does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron pairs its luxury aesthetics with a sporty drive that makes it fun on the road, all while remaining whisper-quiet on the inside thanks to its air-suspension ride and solid soundproofing. While its nearly $95,000 as-tested price tag is a hefty amount, it’s accompanied by premium features and surprisingly efficient for drivers who want sports-sedan thrills without sacrificing everyday versatility.

Smooth ride and punchy acceleration.

Hefty cost puts it out of the budget of most people.

Awkwardly placed cruise control stalk.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

When I got into the driver's seat of the Audi A6 Sportback e-tron last year, my expectations weren’t all that high. But it ended up impressing me so much that it quickly became one of the best electric cars I’ve tested. With the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron, it’s pretty evident that Audi has dialed up the aggression and sportier flair.

Recent findings suggest that while there are similarities between the two, the S6 Sportback e-tron differentiates itself with standard dual-motor quattro all-wheel drive, sport-tuned adaptive air suspension, and up to 543 horsepower. Quite simply, it’s a mid-size luxury sedan that trades some range for extra muscle.

I tested the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron Prestige for a week, which carries a $94,490 as-tested price — putting it squarely in the crosshairs of similar models I’ve tested, like the BMW i5 and Lucid Air Touring. And after seven days behind the wheel, I discovered this pricier performance variant still holds a few surprises up its sleeve.

2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron Prestige.

Dual Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (AWD).

According to recent reports, I drove the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron Prestige for a total of 152.4 miles and recorded an overall average efficiency of 3.6 mi/kWh. While that overall figure trails slightly behind the results I got out of the BMW i5 and Lucid Air Touring, it’s well within striking range of its main rivals.

Personally, I think it’s a valiant result given how the A6 Sportback e-tron yielded 3.7 mi/kWh in my previous test. On longer highway stretches, I’ve recorded a best mark of 3.9 mi/kWh with the A6 Sportback — while short trip efficiency reached 3.6 mi/kWh.

When plugged into a standard household outlet for Level 1 charging, the S6 Sportback e-tron added range at a rate of 4.05 miles per hour. That places it squarely in the middle of its rivals, beating the Lucid Air Touring while trailing the BMW i5 xDrive40.

2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron Prestige.

Best long distance driving efficiency.

Best short distance driving efficiency.

I’ve always been a fan of Audi’s signature design philosophy, and the 2027 S6 Sportback e-tron takes that familiar luxury aesthetic and injects it with an aggressive, sporty edge. Between its low-slung fastback silhouette, razor-sharp LED lighting, and glossy front grille, it strikes an athletic stance that never feels overdone — and makes me feel young at heart.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Behind the wheel, the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron delivers a refined, whisper-quiet ride that glides effortlessly over rough pavement thanks to its standard sport adaptive air suspension. Yet the moment I bury my foot in the accelerator, it pins me back in the seat with blistering off-the-line speed.

In a recent development, that effortless torque makes overtaking slower traffic on the highway feel almost instantaneous, giving me serious passing power without ever sacrificing its composed demeanor. It actually offers a better ride than the Lucid Air and matches the BMW i5 on open roads.

One of the standout tech features on the S6 Sportback e-tron is Audi's augmented reality head-up display, which projects crisp visuals directly into my line of sight on the windshield. Beyond showing me all the usual stats — like my current speed, turn-by-turn navigation arrows, and speed limit signs — it also visualizes adaptive cruise assist and following distance in real time.

It’s one of the most comprehensive and advanced HUDs out there, even turning red when the gap to the vehicle ahead gets too short.

It has been revealed that in 2026, it’s still very rare for any vehicle to come with an integrated dashcam, but the S6 Sportback e-tron is one of them. Ingeniously, it’s built into the auto-dimming rearview mirror — keeping the windshield free of clutter, unlike third-party camera solutions with dangling power cables. Not only does it offer automatic loop recording for convenience, but it also doesn’t require an extra fee or subscription just to work.

Recent findings suggest that another practical advantage of the S6 Sportback e-tron is its rear liftback design, which opens up a massive cargo hold that puts conventional sedans to shame. Unlike the traditional, narrower trunk openings I dealt with on the BMW i5 and Lucid Air Touring, the Audi’s entire rear glass lifts with the power tailgate — making it far easier to load bulky gear, luggage, or larger items that simply wouldn’t clear a standard trunk lid.

With roughly 26 cubic feet of space behind the second row (and even more when you fold the rear seats flat), it gives you crossover-like versatility wrapped in a sleek sport-sedan profile.

I’ll be the first to admit that its $95,000 as-tested price is hefty, but Audi compensates for it with a serious tech suite of luxury features you don’t traditionally find. Overhead, the panoramic glass roof features variable light control that electronically lets me switch between transparent and opaque at the touch of a button, while LED interior ambient lighting wraps across the dashboard and brings the cabin to life at night.

In a recent development, on the outside, I love small details like the animations of the LED headlights and OLED taillights, which give it a slick look when turning the vehicle on and off. There are also dual charging ports on either side of the vehicle, giving me the convenience of parking however I want for Level 1 and 2 charging — albeit with Level 3 DC fast charging only supported on the driver’s side.

Entertainment and audio get just as much attention, thanks to a crisp 10.9-inch front passenger display and a booming Bang & Olufsen 3D sound system that even builds speakers directly into the front headrests.

While the S6 Sportback e-tron’s sleek, low-slung roofline looks fantastic from the outside, it comes at the expense of a narrower rear windshield compared to its rivals. As a result, it creates a somewhat letterbox-like view.

Between the low roofline, chunky A-pillars, and the large sensor housing behind the rearview mirror, spotting overhead traffic lights can be challenging when pulling up close to an intersection.

Sources indicate that I’m the kind of driver who religiously activates adaptive cruise control, and while I appreciate how the S6 Sportback e-tron keeps steady in its lane, it lacks automatic lane-change assist. That means I’m still forced to manually take over whenever I want to pass slower traffic on the highway — a glaring omission for a pricey $95K luxury vehicle.

Industry observers note that compounding that frustration is how Audi continues to put all of the adaptive cruise control functions on a dedicated stalk tucked behind the lower left side of the steering wheel, which forces me to move my hand slightly away from the wheel. I’d much rather have them integrated into one of the control pads on the steering wheel itself.

There’s a lot to love about the 2027 Audi S6 Sportback e-tron, starting with its sharp and sporty design, all the way to its genuinely practical hatchback-like utility. Add in a rich roster of high-end comfort tech — from its augmented reality HUD to its built-in dashcam — it delivers an upscale daily driving experience.

According to recent reports, still, at nearly $95,000 as tested, that steep price tag makes it a tough pill to swallow for most buyers, especially when smaller quirks like a narrow windshield and inconveniently placed cruise-control stalk hold it back from perfection. If you don't need the extra cargo space or blistering acceleration and are willing to go a little smaller, the 2027 Mercedes-Benz CLA 250+ delivers exceptional luxury EV value at a dramatically lower price.

Here’s a HomeView feature that should come to every Apple device

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, this week, Apple started shipping the HomeView, its first display made for the smart home.
  • On iOS, iPadOS, and macOS today – the only flexibility you have on dark mode is whether or not it automatically switches on towards night time.
  • With HomeView, you can enable ambient dark mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this week, Apple started shipping the HomeView, its first display made for the smart home. On the HomeView, there’s one particularly nice feature that I’d love to see make its way to all Apple platforms: Ambient Dark Mode.

On iOS, iPadOS, and macOS today – the only flexibility you have on dark mode is whether or not it automatically switches on towards night time. While this is generally helpful and certainly appreciated, it isn’t super granular. Of course, you can adjust the time when it switches, but generally speaking its just a one time toggle.

With HomeView, you can enable ambient dark mode. In display settings, once you enable automatic dark mode, there’s the usual two settings you’d see on other Apple platforms: sunrise to sunset, as well as a custom schedule. HomeView takes it a step further with ambient mode, where the ambient light sensor determines whether or not you should be in light or dark mode.

Of course, a sunrise to sunset schedule generally works for most cases. However, if you’re up late at night with your lights turned on, you still might prefer light mode in an instance where macOS would generally be in dark mode. Similarly, if you wake up later in the day with your curtains shut, at say 11am, you might not want to immediately see light mode on your phone the second you open your eyes.

There are tons of good reasons for why someone would prefer ambient light-based automatic light and dark mode switching. HomeView software is the first Apple platform to enable this, and I’d love to see it come to iPhone, iPad, and Mac starting next year with OS 28.

  • “Selena is pleased by today’s dismissal of the case following our motion to dismiss and looks forward to putting the matter behind her,” her lawyer Mathew S.
  • Recent findings suggest that an attorney for Pierson, Scott Balber, tells Rolling Stone that they did not pay any settlement in the case.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lawsuit accusing Selena Gomez, her mother Mandy Teefey, and The Newsette founder, Daniella Pierson, of defrauding investors behind the mental health startup Wondermind has been dropped after her attorneys filed a motion to dismiss the case.

“Selena is pleased by today’s dismissal of the case following our motion to dismiss and looks forward to putting the matter behind her,” her lawyer Mathew S. Rosengart said in a statement to Rolling Stone. According to documents, the plaintiffs “voluntarily” dismissed the lawsuit.

Recent findings suggest that an attorney for Pierson, Scott Balber, tells Rolling Stone that they did not pay any settlement in the case. “Ms. Pierson did nothing wrong,” noted Balber. “Apparently, the plaintiff recognized that and dismissed the complaint against her. Unfortunately, Ms. Pierson’s reputation has already been damaged by these false allegations. We are hopeful that the dismissal of the lawsuit will be the first step in restoring her good name.”.

It has been revealed that in August, Gomez, Teefey, and Pierson were sued by investors claiming they pumped nearly $1.2 million into Wondermind, which introduced in 2021, and were fed false promises about the company’s infrastructure, leadership, and resources as the company collapsed. The trio, who founded the startup, were sued for securities fraud, common law fraud, and breach of contract.

In the lawsuit, investors alleged they were led to believe that a groundbreaking Wondermind app would be made, advertising deals would be struck, and celebrity cover stories were pending. Instead, the complaint claimed, “for three years, while the Company quietly collapsed around them, not one of its founders, officers, or directors noted a word to the investors whose money was funding the collapse.” Trending Stories Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Cynthia Erivo, Travis Barker Honor Phil Collins With Big Vocals, Big Drums at Rock Hall Ceremony Miley Cyrus Shares Sweet Memory of Godmother Dolly Parton as They Earn a Grammy Nod Together.

In the motion to dismiss, Gomez’s legal team stated she should have never been dragged into the case in the first place. Her lawyers added that while the star “agreed to support her mother Mandy Teefey” and invested in and holds a minority stake in Wondermind, Gomez “never agreed to and did not manage” the organization.

In a previous statement to Rolling Stone, Rosengart mentioned the claims against her were “completely meritless if not frivolous.” He added, “The notion that Selena engaged in ‘fraud’ or any other wrongdoing is absurd—and in addition to filing our motion we are exploring other avenues of relief for Ms. Gomez including sanctions against plaintiffs for improperly including her.”.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the latest Apple Watches have a lot of newly introduced features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • According to recent reports, the Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • Recent findings suggest that you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the latest Apple Watches have a lot of newly introduced features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

According to recent reports, the Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is currently in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

Industry observers note that to finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own important details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

First, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

It has been revealed that the double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

If you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

Industry observers note that A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the new AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri launches into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

According to recent reports, if you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in September, Apple introduced the new Beats 360 headphones, the first overears from Beats since the Beats Studio Pro in 2023.
  • One of the biggest differences between the two will be the price.
  • Despite being older and cheaper, the Beats Studio Pro have a couple advantages over the Beats 360.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in September, Apple introduced the new Beats 360 headphones, the first overears from Beats since the Beats Studio Pro in 2023. That said, the older Beats Studio Pro still remain on sale at a lower price point – so it begs the question, which Beats headphones are more worthwhile?

One of the biggest differences between the two will be the price. The Beats Studio Pro, since they’re older, are regularly available on discount. Right now, you can pick up Beats Studio Pro for $199-249 on Amazon, compared to Beats 360, which aren’t discounted from their $349 launch pricing.

Despite being older and cheaper, the Beats Studio Pro have a couple advantages over the Beats 360. On top of the fact that they’re $100-150 cheaper, you may very well still want to consider them.

Industry observers note that the biggest advantages, in my view, have to do with the form factor. The Beats Studio Pro can fold down into a much more compact size, whereas Beats 360 don’t fold at all. This means it’s easier to carry around the Beats Studio Pro.

Beats Studio Pro also offer a headphone jack, whereas Beats 360 don’t have any sort of wired audio at all, even over USB-C. This means Beats Studio Pro are easier to use in environments where bluetooth audio isn’t convenient, such as with a game console or on an airplane.

One of my favorite things about the Beats 360 is that they offer UltraPlush cushions you can swap into, but those cost extra. Beats Studio Pro by default come with UltraPlush cushions, so you can have a more comfortable experience out of the box.

Sources indicate that of course, Beats 360 are newer, so by default they do a number of things better. That includes:.

Out of everything on this list, I’d say clearer transparency, stronger noise cancellation, and automatic device switching make the biggest difference. In my testing, its hard to hear with the transparency mode on the Beats Studio Pro, so I end up taking the headphones off to have conversation. With Beats 360, that isn’t the case.

Sources indicate that as for noise cancellation and automatic device switching, I feel that if you’re buying Beats for the sake of having Apple headphones, you should buy the ones that offer true automatic device switching – and those are the Beats 360. Noise cancellation is more of a personal preference, but if you value having the best noise cancellation, the Beats 360 are noticeably better.

Sources indicate that lastly, the Beats 360 do have the customizable design going for them. While customization is more aesthetically pleasing, it also has an advantage longer term – when the earcups start wearing down over the years, you can quickly replace them on the Beats 360.

While it’s hard to overlook the fact that Beats Studio Pro come in at a much lower price point, I’d generally say that if you want a great pair of headphones that offer an Apple experience, you probably shouldn’t buy the Beats Studio Pro. The Beats Studio Pro are a fine pair of headphones for the price, but you certainly aren’t getting all of the same ecosystem creature comforts that Beats 360 offer.

That said, Beats 360 simply do not offer a headphone jack or a foldable design, and if those things matter to you, then Beats Studio Pro might still be the way to go. Beats Studio Pro also offer a ton of different color options that aren’t available on Beats 360, while costing $150 less.

#16274. Latest Update: 10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1350 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1350 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it.
  • With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does.
  • In a recent development, it seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it. While the newest update isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

In a recent development, it seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2. When you're using an app while running this latest patch, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

While you can load up multiple complications on your Apple Watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a big fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which enhancement dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the latest Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

Industry observers note that to use the Siri Modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the Plus button, and find and add the Siri Modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

The double-tap gesture is one of my favorite Apple Watch features. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

In a recent development, your Apple Watch's latest Music Recognition app has native Shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

It seems like Apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a Coldplay song instantly, even when in Airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

Recent findings suggest that apple Watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. But even still, these apps never showed live data. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

Now, if you own the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or the Ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the Apple Watch face or the Smart Stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the latest Step count widget.

Siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

Recent findings suggest that the Siri AI app on the iPhone indicates all your conversations, and so does the Apple Watch. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

In a recent development, the new Find My app on the Apple Watch reveals a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

According to recent reports, after opening the app, you can use the Digital Crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

While it's not a Whoop-level feature, the Apple Watch now includes a Readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

The Readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it claims; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. You can use the upcoming Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

Low Power Mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your Apple Watch. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 come with a set of Audio Intelligence features that use the microphones on the Apple Watch, paired with AI models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this new feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

Recent findings suggest that sound Recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iPhone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.

Industry observers note that independent oil and natural gas organization Permian Resources (PR) is this week's first dividend stock. The company recently paid a quarterly base cash dividend of 16 cents per share. At an annualized dividend of 64 cents per share, PR offers a dividend yield of 3.5%.

Industry News: I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • Industry observers note that the significant AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

Industry observers note that the significant AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for customers is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

Accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all owners that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

These ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

To set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI says users accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

Gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

Industry observers note that for all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health issues like eating disorders.

In a recent development, these protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

It has been revealed that as with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly quickly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

Industry observers note that meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

If you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

Recent findings suggest that meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All customers, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

According to recent reports, apple users have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

Industry observers note that anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

In a recent development, the new and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

It has been revealed that if your teens are in your family group of customers, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

It has been revealed that like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Owners must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

Recent findings suggest that if you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft states customers identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

More generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

In a recent development, yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

According to recent reports, there is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires users to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

Claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide users towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic says it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

Sources indicate that that's something of a whistle-stop tour of the major seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

  • Patch, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration unveiled it has ended the ground stop.
  • Industry observers note that on Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States.
  • There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patch, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration unveiled it has ended the ground stop.

Industry observers note that on Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

In a recent development, alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

It has been revealed that at this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for people of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

Sources indicate that this is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system issue; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that apple released the all-upcoming MacBook Neo earlier this year, and it’s been a resounding success by all indications. Here’s everything we know so far about what’s next for Apple’s most affordable laptop ….

According to recent reports, the current MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip, which is the same chip used in the iPhone 16 Pro. As reported by Bloomberg, Apple is working on a next-generation MacBook Neo powered by the A19 Pro chip.

In terms of performance, the A19 Pro is about 10-15% faster than the A18 Pro in single-core and multi-core CPU tests. The jump in GPU performance is even bigger, with benchmarks showing an up to 40% boost for the A19 Pro. This is because every GPU core in the A19 Pro has Neural Accelerators built in.

The A19 Pro chip is also used in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Air.

Recent findings suggest that according to reporter Tim Culpan, Apple will likely use a “binned” version of the A19 Pro chip in the MacBook Neo. While the A19 Pro chip in the iPhone 17 Pro has a 6-core GPU, the MacBook Neo version of the chip will likely have a 5-core GPU.

One of the compromises of the MacBook Neo is that it has 8GB of RAM. The rest of Apple’s Mac lineup nowadays starts with 16GB of RAM.

The next-generation MacBook Neo won’t jump all the way to 16GB of RAM. Instead, it’s expected to offer 12GB of RAM thanks to the aforementioned A19 Pro.

Industry observers note that as I wrote in my review, I don’t think it’s a huge limitation that the MacBook Neo has just 8GB of RAM. Still, an increase for the next-generation model is a great improvement.

Sources indicate that the combination of the A19 Pro chip and 12GB of RAM upgrades should also unlock support for Apple’s more powerful on-device AI model confirmed at WWDC. This model enables a more accurate dictation experience and upcoming options for customizing the Siri voice.

The current MacBook Neo doesn’t support this feature because of its A18 Pro chip and 8GB of RAM.

Industry observers note that the MacBook Neo is available in an array of fun colors, including citrus, blush, indigo, and silver. Bloomberg reports that Apple’s plan is to “periodically” update the MacBook Neo with newly introduced colors.

There aren’t any details on which colors the next-generation MacBook Neo will be available in.

Apple released the current MacBook Neo in March. Tim Culpan reports that the A19 Pro version of the machine is slated for a release sometime in 2027.

When it comes to 3-in-1 travel chargers, I look at two main things: How fast it can charge my iPhone and how portable it is. I have tested plenty of travel chargers that aim to be as portable as possible by using lightweight materials or folding into a smaller footprint, but there usually seems to be some sort of compromise. But this latest K4 Air by Kuxiu might be the most impressive option I’ve tested to date. This charger is just 8.5mm thin, weighs less than 120 g, and can wirelessly charge your iPhone at up to 25W. After spending a few weeks with it and traveling across the Atlantic, here is what you should know about the Kuxiu K4 Air.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video with the K4 Air to see it in action!

The biggest selling point of the newly introduced Kuxiu K4 Air is its design. When completely folded, this thing is barely thicker than an iPhone. For reference, my iPhone 17 Pro measures roughly 8.25mm thick, while the K4 Air comes in at just 8.5mm. That is insanely compact for something that can charge three devices at once. And even though they went ultra-slim, they did not really need to sacrifice any charging performance. You get:.

Sources indicate that one of my favorite things about Kuxiu has always been their price-to-performance ratio. While some brands and companies are removing charging bricks and even cables, Kuxiu is adding a ton of value here by including everything you need directly in the packaging. The build quality of the charger is also fantastic. It feels balanced, well-made, and extremely versatile because of all the situations you can use it in.

Kuxiu has also done a great job of bringing us a Burgundy color option that perfectly matches the newly introduced Burgundy iPhone color. I wish Apple would continue making the Cosmic Orange iPhone because the K4 Air in that orange would have been awesome.

According to recent reports, I recommend watching our video to see my reaction when I pick up the K4 Air for the first time. I was shocked at how small it was. It was thin and lightweight, but still felt solid because it was made of metal and not plastic. The form factor and size make it incredibly easy to throw into any bag, pocket, purse, or even just leave it attached to your iPhone for when it is needed.

Industry observers note that the charging experience is actually pretty straightforward. You unfold the charger, connect the USB-C cable, and you’re ready to go. The main magnetic charging surface supports your iPhone, while the second surface is for AirPods. They even added magnets to the AirPods charging pad to ensure they stay in place every single time. There is also a dedicated Apple Watch charger that folds down to charge any Apple Watch. I was charging my Apple Watch Ultra 4, and it fit perfectly.

But now the major question: how well does it work with the iPhone Duo? Personally, I charge my iPhone Duo on my nightstand charger when it is folded shut. So I have zero issues with it. But if you open the iPhone, place it on the charger in landscape mode, and then use it, it will tilt slightly to the left. But to my surprise, if you use the iPhone Duo and open it in portrait mode, it works great! The charger doubles as a stand and easily supports the iPhone Duo. Another cool piece that the form factor unlocks is that it can technically charge two iPhones at the same time, so if you are in a pinch, you can charge two iPhones at once,.

So, regardless of which iPhone you are using, as long as it supports MagSafe, you are good to go. But how much does something like this cost?

Sources indicate that the Kuxiu K4 Air is finally back in stock after a limited initial run. You can get it on Kuxiu’s website for $79. It comes in Space Gray and their newly introduced Burgundy color. As I mentioned above, you also get the charging cable, a 45W charging brick, and a carrying pouch.

Personally, I am a huge fan of how good the Burgundy color looks.

After using the Kuxiu K4 Air, it is just one of those accessories that makes sense. It is small, compact, lightweight, and extremely useful. It fits perfectly into the travel charger category. There are a ton of great 3-in-1 chargers, with fresh ones flooding the market daily, but very few combine this level of portability with all the features we discussed.

In a recent development, so if you are shopping for a portable 3-in-1 travel charger for yourself or as a gift, I would highly recommend giving this one a shot. It’s well-built, charges your big three Apple products, and looks fantastic.

#16260. Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (789 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let customers scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Google says it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for people whose data was found on the dark web.
  • It has been revealed that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let people run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let customers scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the company discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with new scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Google says it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for people whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a new service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

It has been revealed that dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let people run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google launched the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One people, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

Recent findings suggest that you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

In a recent development, it’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

Industry observers note that but perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that owners want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the manufacturer hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

According to recent reports, many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

According to recent reports, there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

In a recent development, if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

According to recent reports, finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

Industry News: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on the Claude Code team, the vast majority of our code (~90%) is written and reviewed by Claude.
  • Verification loops are the building block that lets you delegate more work to Claude.
  • Thatâs because giving agents a way to verify their output is an effective way to improve quality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on the Claude Code team, the vast majority of our code (~90%) is written and reviewed by Claude. At this scale, how we equip our agents to verify their work with evidence becomes extremely crucial.

Verification loops are the building block that lets you delegate more work to Claude. Without them, you can really only run one or two Claudes at a time, because you have to check everything yourself. With them, you can run dozens or hundreds in parallel.

Thatâs because giving agents a way to verify their output is an effective way to improve quality. In internal testing around structured file generation, having a separate grader check Claudeâs work against a rubric improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop, with the largest gains on the hardest problems.

What was once expensive to verify (tests, benchmarks, specs, real end-to-end runs) is now cheap to request from an agent. Like code, agents can quickly generate tests, benchmarks, and specs. And once generated, these tests and benchmarks run as software so they can be run frequently without using many additional tokens.

According to recent reports, you can also close the verification loop by using the results to improve the agentâs performance on that task. For example, if an agent repeatedly fails a test that checks logs for user data, you can create a hook or a more explicit rule in your CLAUDE.md to avoid future issues. This (mostly) stops issues from happening again.

Sources indicate that so if verification is critical to producing quality code at a high velocity, what types of tests should you use and how should you apply them across your pipeline? This article answers those questions and also shares the process used by the Claude Code team.

No matter which test type you choose, there are a few failure modes to avoid.

Recent findings suggest that if your tests are flaky youâll train the agent to run them again rather than fixing the failing code. If your tests are slow, the agent will do fewer tests across batches which can make pinpointing problems difficult. Heavier tests are best deployed before youâve committed the changes.

Now, here are the three types of tests I think are most worth investing in.

If you have to focus on one test type, pick end-to-end. These tests describe real user flows like adding an item to a cart, checking out, and moving to a confirmation page.

The reason E2E tests are so effective is that they are difficult to foolâeither the whole feature works or it doesn't. They also have definitive done criteria and can concretely tell you whatâs broken.

According to recent reports, while unit tests are faster and less flaky, itâs possible to pass them and still break the feature. This is because both the agent and the test donât understand the full task.

Industry observers note that with E2E tests, it is effective to give your agent hands and eyes on the real running system. You can use a skill to boot, drive, and inspect the app with tools like CDP, simulators, or API harnesses.

The feature map can serve as a guide and grading rubric for agents as they typically list features from the userâs point of view with descriptions of paths, keyboard shortcuts, selectors, and expected results.

In a recent development, A lot of tests are based on what you thought might go wrong. Property tests look at the edge cases that people tend to miss, which is where agents often fail.

You start by writing a statement you think canât fail and then use a test library (fast-check for JS/TS, Hypothesis for Python, proptest for Rust, etc.) to generate thousands of inputs that try to prove otherwise.

There are many properties in virtually every software project like:.

It has been revealed that property libraries are a great way to keep agents honest by using edge cases that arenât created with the same bias as the agent that created the original code. They are also particularly helpful for rewrites when the spec has drifted from production behavior and is no longer a reliable source for verification.

Differential tests are particularly effective for large-scale migration use cases where functionality is expected to remain the same. For these tests, you run both the old system and the new system with the same inputs and see if you get different results. If you do, there is a bug or breaking change that needs to be fixed.

The key for differential tests is to use randomly generated inputs or a sample of production traffic. Youâll also want to normalize irrelevant factors like whitespace and keep a list of approved changes for situations where the new environment should differ from the old.

We have previously written about how code review works at Anthropic, but this article aims to go deeper on how we verify our work.

Running the app end to end matters more than tests. You wouldn't ship an iOS change without trying it in a simulator, and the same goes for Claude.

Industry observers note that claude can test the whole app the way a human or QA engineer would. Ask it to use the Claude Chrome extension for web changes, an iOS or Android MCP for mobile, computer use for desktop, or to run the service locally for backend work.

In a recent development, to codify how to start the simulator or run your app, create a skill called verify. Put it in a .claude/skills/ folder in your repo, as close to the relevant code as you can, and add as many as you need. Claude knows to use the verify skill before committing changes.

Then invest in making your verify skill fast and reliable. Ask Claude to iterate on it and stress test it. It's your smoke test harness, so you want it rock solid.

When you give Claude a way to smoke test its changes end to end, you get much better results. You'll see it iterate and catch real mistakes faster, the way a human would. This is how we test nearly all changes at Anthropic.

According to recent reports, nobody can read every change, so we use failures as one way to decide what needs a person. Claude runs the checks and tries to fix anything that fails. If a check is still failing after three rounds, Claude stops and brings in a human.

Recent findings suggest that the people who own the code write the checks for it, and refine them until they flag what the owner would flag. When a check pulls in a reviewer, it should say why, so they don't have to work it out from the diff.

According to recent reports, we maintain a reliability checklist with 39 items, each with a trigger that can be read from a diff, a check, and the incidents or PRs behind it. One is â--resume loads old transcripts.â When session storage or message types change, we ask whether a fresh field loads safely, since older transcripts wonât have it.

Claude reads the diff and checks only the items whose trigger matchesâusually 3 to 10âso nobody has to memorize past outages.

We don't try to improve reviews by stacking on more reviewers. Adding a second, more expensive, reviewer on top of the primary one is often a worse approach than tuning the primary. Instead, we have a REVIEW.md that indicates what the reviewer should pay attention to for this code.

Industry observers note that we also think review and verification rounds should build on each other. We point each pass at context from earlier rounds and past failures rather than re-checking everything from scratch. Itâs cheaper and finds more.

According to recent reports, if a change can modify the check that judges it, the check is broken. Code Review reads the REVIEW.md file from the base or default branch, never from the pull request's changes. The Claude Code team ensures the rules that gate changes are on a branch that the change can't modify.

The Claude Code team also reserves reviews for commits. If someone's pushing while the review is happening, then the review result is no longer useful. A passing review on an out-of-date commit means nothing.

The team also runs cheap checks first. If an agent pushes before testing locally, it has spent shared review and CI time when it could have caught the bug itself. On our team, Claude runs the tests, build, and linter before opening a pull request. You can enforce this with a hook that runs the tests when Claude finishes, or a /goal of a passing test suite.

Recent findings suggest that in our own repos, we stamp each commit with how it was verified. The stamp even includes "none" so we can query for commits that weren't verified.

We've also created a commit gate that can block a commit if the session did not contain /code-review or /verify. We've set it up with off, observe, and enforce modes.

Observe mode will log what would have been blocked, so that we can review any false positives and ensure no one is impacted.

Enforce mode will block the commit. Any commit can carry an explanation in its message as to why it didn't get verified. If commits have been blocked twice in the session, the next one will be allowed through so Claude doesn't get stuck â Claude Code isn't perfect.

The Claude Code team also regularly reviews the reviewers. We track how many merged changes were reverted, how many changes a maintainer rejected before merging, and a size-matched subset of changes that have stayed clean.

This can also be done with a formal evaluation. In our code review post, we described how the Code Review team has set up an evaluation based on previous incidents and reverts. They recreate the repo to the state at the time of review for each example, and provide a one-sentence answer key to what the bug was. Only findings that correctly describe the bug in question get points. They use merged and stable changes as a control to prevent over-flagging. Their tuning set is split out from the fixed test set they use to evaluate their system.

It has been revealed that they also evaluated the recall rate for raw findings, post-verification, and final review separately. This lets them see if the system is losing bugs it had already found. Any evaluation that treats all these as one end-to-end score won't capture this nuance.

It has been revealed that in addition to validity, the other dimension we care about is how notable it is to make the change. A good reviewer will catch most things that are technically correct, but people care about whether a given bug is a must-fix, a should-fix, or a nit.

It has been revealed that code Review has this exact idea, and it will tag things as Important, Nit or Pre-existing. The "pre-existing" tag means that the reviewer shouldn't hold the author responsible for something that was already a bug.

Finally, the Claude Code team tunes recall up to the point where the next improvement would be overfitting to the eval rather than actually catching bugs.

According to recent reports, in the Claude Code repo, we have two methods of turning missed cases into rules. The first is extracting patterns in human code review comments and PR reverts to identify common issues. These must occur in at least two PRs and be identifiable from a diff to be considered a potential rule. Three agents will try to disprove them, and they will be reviewed and approved by a human in a PR.

According to recent reports, the second method is replaying three bug finders against a PR that is associated with a known incident. If at least two find the bug, it's a detectable bug. If the bug is missed on a small diff, this is a gap that is worth turning into a rule in REVIEW.md.

Recent findings suggest that flaky tests get the same treatment. Claude can't skip them, add sleeps or retry until they pass. If it can't find the root cause, it deletes the test and writes down why.

Industry observers note that rules need cleaning up too. Test suites, verification steps and .md files only grow if you let them, so we tidy them up on a routine.

Weâve found that giving your agent a way to verify its work with a strong feedback loop makes all the difference. Treat your verification layer like you would any other system. Keep it out of reach of the changes they judge, grade them against the bugs that mattered to you, and write down lessons when they miss something so that it doesnât happen more than once, and prune those lessons so they stay worth running.

Do that and your job shifts from reading every diff to defining what âdoneâ looks like and reviewing the evidence, which is what lets you run many Claudes at once.

The best Apple Watches are capable of some pretty remarkable things, like sending for help if you take a nasty fall, predicting your daily readiness, and logging physical fitness.

But with so much capability, some of the most useful Apple Watch tools and apps inevitably fly under the radar. That's where I come in. I'm Dan, and I lead TG's smartwatch review coverage. I'm also an avid Apple Watch wearer with strong opinions and a knack for tinkering with settings.

With that in mind, here are five favorite lesser-known Apple Watch features that I absolutely swear by. Some were added via the recent watchOS 27 release, while others are old standbys.

Note: This list expands my previously published 7 hidden Apple Watch features I swear by round-up from earlier in the year.

Dividing up a check between friends can be a tedious task, especially if you and your pals aren't math whizzes. If only there were a super-simple way to calculate a tip and split a check without breaking a sweat.

There is! Your Apple Watch's boring old Calculator app features a built-in tip button. Simply enter the total amount of the check and tap "Tip." This brings up a screen where you can enter your desired tip percentage and the number of individuals paying for an instant calculation.

And just like that, you'll never fumble a check again.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Apple first introduced the double-tap gesture control for Apple Watch back in 2023. Simply tap your index finger and thumb together twice on your watch-wearing wrist to execute actions like answering a call, closing an app, stopping a timer, or pausing a song.

In 2026, Apple added a single-tap gesture that works in exactly the same way, minus the second tap. To set it up, head to Settings > Gestures. Super-useful, I have my double-tap programmed to open the Smart Stack, while the single-tap opens my most recent/active widget, all without interacting with the screen or buttons.

When it comes to on-wrist safety, I'd argue that Apple and Google lead the pack, and one of my favorite Apple Watch personal safety features, Check In, often gets overlooked.

It has been revealed that check In is a reliable and simple way to keep friends and/or loved ones looped into your location at critical times. For example, I can set a Check In when I leave my apartment that automatically alerts my partner when I arrive at my set destination.

Industry observers note that or, if you're an avid runner, you can use the feature to automatically keep those you trust informed of when you both depart and arrive safely back home. Here's a deeper dive into how to use one of Apple's best safety features.

While on the subject of safety, I'd be remiss not to mention Apple's equally valuable Backtrack safety feature, which is particularly useful when exploring new places, if for nothing else, peace of mind.

Backtrack works like a digital breadcrumb trail, allowing you to retrace your steps back to your starting location via turn-by-turn directions in the event you get lost. Best of all, it works both in urban environments and out in nature.

Here's more on how to set up and use Apple's Backtrack tool.

Last but not least, and perhaps the easiest to miss, we have Apple's silent, vibration-based alarm clock. This is by no means a new feature, but it's one I adore and use daily.

As a U.S. West Coast-based writer with colleagues primarily in New York and London, my days tend to start quite early. Rather than risking waking my sleep partner or puppy, I schedule my alarm and set my Apple Watch 12 to silent. This switches the wake-up alert from an audible one to a vibration-based one, which I also find to be a gentler way to snap into reality.
