AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1035 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • According to recent reports, you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—at the moment at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

According to recent reports, you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—at the moment at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

Industry observers note that as the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

Sources indicate that for the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Recent findings suggest that pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

Sources indicate that what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

It has been revealed that now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

To be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

In a recent development, however, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

Sources indicate that image and video detection is the new string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

Sources indicate that again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

According to recent reports, next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Industry observers note that here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

Recent findings suggest that I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

Sources indicate that as with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran showed that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

It has been revealed that increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An append-only in-memory database in Rust for rows queried using bit (flag) columns.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An append-only in-memory database in Rust for rows queried using bit (flag) columns. This database is designed for a very specific use case where you have mostly static data that you typically load at startup and have to query constantly using very simple filters. Datasets like these can be large and should be both fast and compact.

For the limited usecases where venndb can be applied to, it has next to no dependencies and is faster then traditional choices, such as a naive implementation or a more heavy lifted dependency such as Sqlite.

See the benchmarks for more information on this topic.

According to recent reports, this project was developed originally in function of rama, where you can see it being used for example to provide an in-memory (upstream) proxy database. Do let us know in case you use it as well in your project, such that we can assemble a showcase list.

Benchmarks displayed here are taken on a dev machine with following specs:.

The benchmarks test 4 different implementations of a proxy database, shaped like the one of rama: 7 bool properties and 5 filter maps, of which the state, city and ASN have up to 1 000, 10 000 and 5 000 distinct values.

In a recent development, apart from the first two, each row is a query: the filters listed are set on db.query(), followed by any() to pick a random proxy among the matching ones. The bool filters ask for true, the filter maps (pool, country, city) for one value unless more are mentioned, and 1% of their rows match any value. The numbers are the median time. The benchmarks are created by running just bench-full | python3 scripts/bench_tables.py.

Contributions in the form of Pull requests are welcomed as well, see the Contribution guidelines for more information.

❓ Why use this over Database X?

It has been revealed that venndb is not a database, but is close enough for some specific purposes. It shines for long-lived read-only use cases where you need to filter on plenty of binary properties and get a rando matching result.

Do not try to replace your usual database needs with it.

❓ Where can I propose a newly introduced feature X or some other improvement?

According to recent reports, please open an problem and also read the Contribution guidelines. We look forward to hear from you.

Alternatively you can also join our Discord and start a conversation / discussion over there.

❓ Can I use whatever type for a #[venndb(filter)] property?

Yes, as long as it implements Eq + Hash + Clone. That said, we do recommend that you use enum values if you can, or some other highly restricted form.

It has been revealed that using for example a String directly is a bad idea as that would mean that bE != Be != BE != Belgium != Belgique != België. Even though these are really referring all to the same country. In such cases a much better idea is to at the very least create a wrapper type such as struct Country(String), to allow you to enforce sanitization/validation when creating the value and ensuring the hashes will be the same for those values that are conceptually the same.

❓ How do I make a filter optional?

Both filters (bool properties) and filter maps (T != bool properties with the #[venndb(filter)] attribute) can be made optional by wrapping the types with Option, resulting in Option and Option.

Rows that have the Option::None value for such an optional column cannot filter on that property, but there is no other consequence beyond that.

❓ Why can do keys have to be unique and non-optional?

Within venndb keys are meant to be able to look up, a row which was previously received via filters.

As such it makes no sense for such keys to be:.

❓ How can I allow some rows to match for any value of a certain (filter) column?

Filter maps can allow to have a value to match all other values. It is up to you to declare the filter as such, and to also define for that type what the one value to rule them all is.

For a type that is no enum you implement venndb::Any yourself, and for a type that is not yours you can point to a function instead: #[venndb(filter, any = is_any)].

❓ How can a property have multiple values?

Mark the filter as a set. A row then matches each of the values in it:.

It works for HashSet, BTreeSet and any type implementing venndb::FilterSet, not for lists such as Vec. For a type that is not yours use #[venndb(filter, members = path)], with path a function returning an iterator over the values, and item = "Type" if the type of those cannot be told from the property. Every "filter map" property has a _where method, rows with an any value always match it.

❓ How can I filter on something that is not a property, or that changes?

Create a column for it and add it to the query:.

The first only knows about the rows the database had when it was created, in the second any row can be set at any time: see the runtime example, also for what to do when the database is replaced. For a condition that fits no column there is EmployeeDBQueryResult::any_where(predicate).

❓ How can I provide custom validation of rows prior to them getting appended?

Sources indicate that is is possible to validate a row based on one or multiple of its properties? Validate in function of relationship between multiple properties? Is it possible to provide custom validation to prevent rows from getting appended that do not adhere to custom validation rules?

❓ Why do any filter values only match rows that have an any value for that property?

Let's say I have the following struct:.

Industry observers note that why is this true? Because it is correct.

Sources indicate that allowing it also to match the value foo would unfairly give more chances for foo to be selected over the any value. This might not seem like a significant difference, but it is. Because what if we generate a random string for Values with an _any value? If we would allow all rows to be matched then that logic is now rigged, with a value of foo being more likely then other strings.

As such the only correct answer when filtering for any value, is to return rows that have any value.

❓ How can I query on multiple variants of a "filter map" property?

Just call the query method multiple times. It will allow you to match rows that have either of these values.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A growing number of people are asking AI chatbots about their health issues, raising two major concerns: safety and privacy. Apple is now offering a safer way to do this through an Apple Health AI Usage Study.

This is actually one of Apple’s research studies, but those volunteering to take part in it will be able to ask health questions – with three key assurances not guaranteed by other AI chatbots ….

Apple launched its Research app back in 2019 with the goal of allowing customers to help universities and medical institutions with health studies. You typically agree to share certain anonymized information from the Apple Health app in order to provide data that can advance medical research. You may also be asked to complete questionnaires.

It has been revealed that the Apple Health AI Usage Study is one of these, but it works in a somewhat different way. You’ll still be invited to share some of your health data, but will also be able to ask an AI system questions about your health.

It has been revealed that when you ask health questions of a typical AI chatbot, you don’t know how reliable those answers may be or what will happen to your data. Apple study offers three assurances:.

Apple indicates that answers will be generated by the same platform used by healthcare professionals.

The study is conducted in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a leading clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals that generates answers using medical information from established sources such as The Upcoming England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature.

The answers provided to you will include links to peer-reviewed clinical citations.

As you’d expect from Apple, there are strong privacy protections, including the assurance that your data will not be used to train AI models.

Recent findings suggest that the study is designed from the ground up with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and study data will not be used to train AI models. Participants retain control over whether to share any HealthKit metrics or survey responses, and Apple has implemented security measures to protect the study data it maintains, as well as the confidentiality of participants’ information.

CNET reports on Apple’s assurance that none of your chats will be retained.

OpenEvidence will delete both question and response data within 24 hours. A small group of Apple researchers will have access to coded versions of survey responses, separated from personally identifiable information, summaries of conversations and categories of the most common conversation types.

Access to the study is right now limited to people in the US by downloading the app. If you try it, please do share your thoughts in the comments.

Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Industry observers note that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Industry observers note that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully debuted on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Recent findings suggest that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Recent findings suggest that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

According to recent reports, phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

In a recent development, scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

In a recent development, more than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a upcoming rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

Industry observers note that MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to strategy, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

In a recent development, once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to strategy, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” notes Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

Sources indicate that from that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

It has been revealed that during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Industry observers note that before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu notes, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

In a recent development, idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

It has been revealed that “It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

According to recent reports, A simulation reveals how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

In a recent development, once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” states Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

In a recent development, the WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday claims Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Industry observers note that idefix’s interactions with its fresh home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

Recent findings suggest that what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

Recent findings suggest that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel claims. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

Industry observers note that the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this concern and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Sources indicate that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel notes. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Sources indicate that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu claims. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • In a recent development, download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • It has been revealed that install Python on your system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

In a recent development, download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

It has been revealed that install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

In a recent development, run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Recent findings suggest that have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

According to recent reports, like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of upcoming-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

It has been revealed that on Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. People can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

If you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

Industry observers note that plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

Industry observers note that tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

Industry observers note that exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

It has been revealed that mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

Recent findings suggest that my cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

Industry observers note that it's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

In a recent development, your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

You have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

This isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.

There are two main reasons people still buy standalone cameras despite having an iPhone in their pocket wherever they go. The first is lens quality: iPhones have small plastic lenses compared to the far larger and more sophisticated glass lenses used with dedicated cameras.

Sources indicate that the second is sensor size. All other things being equal, a larger sensor will capture more light and provide a higher quality image. Current smartphone sensors are absolutely tiny compared to those used in even mid-range consumer cameras.

This is less likely to be an matter with a telephoto lens, which is normally used outdoors rather than inside.

What I’d really love to see is a significantly larger sensor for the main camera, with no increase in resolution. This would improve low light performance and overall image quality.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it's time to do a bit of extra research into your finances, AI tools like ChatGPT’s Finances dashboard exist to help you do just that (as long as you trust it enough to connect your financial accounts to it through Plaid).

Recent findings suggest that it doesn’t come as much of a surprise that Gemini has decided to join in on that trend. Google has already begun rolling out Google Wallet as the last connected app to become integrated into Gemini—US consumers now have the ability to use this feature to get informed responses on their finances based on the linked credit card and bank accounts attached to their Google Wallet profile via Plaid.

Sources indicate that turning Google Wallet on inside Gemini is as simple as clicking on the “Settings” icon (which is the gear wheel that sits across from your Google account name and photo), selecting “Personal Intelligence,” clicking “Connected Apps” and adding the Google Wallet connector. From that point forward, you can prompt the connector by starting your inquiry with “@Google Wallet.”.

Thankfully, Gemini’s Google Wallet powers exist only to give you financial insight—it will never move, manage or invest any of the money attached to your linked accounts. To get the best insights, it’s worth trying out any of the following prompts to see just how helpful it can be.

I decided to ask Gemini itself about the sort of basic questions anyone willing to try its Google Wallet-connected app should ask. Google’s chatbot came back to me with a collection of readily usable prompts—here are 10 that you should keep in your digital back pocket for yourself and anyone else you know who might want to try them out for themselves:.

The first prompt gets straight to the point, as it scans your linked transaction history to check for any recurring charges and flag any sudden price increases you might have missed.

Sources indicate that the second prompt investigates your cash flow, producing a dynamic spending chart while pointing out which purchasing categories you may need to cut back on. The third prompt examines your holiday spending trends from the year prior to see how much you may need to save for the current year’s holiday expenses.

The fourth prompt highlights all the frequent tap-to-pay purchases you might have made on eating out compared to your grocery spending, which could compel you to ease up on dining out so much and look for cheaper alternatives while shopping.

Industry observers note that the fifth prompt goes the extra mile to see if any of your linked accounts have any active offers that you can take advantage of before you make a purchase. The sixth prompt makes finding your boarding pass while you’re at a check-in counter and looking up your loyalty numbers while booking a flight so much quicker.

Sources indicate that the seventh prompt works across Gemini’s Personal Intelligence “Memory Summary” feature, your connected Google Wallet and your Gmail to compare what you bought (via email receipts) with how much you spent (via bank/card account info). That way, you can see if you're close or far away from meeting the financial goals you’ve told Gemini about.

According to recent reports, the eighth prompt works great as a visual aid since Gemini can generate dynamic charts for you and give you an easy-to-follow visualization of how your money is distributed across your checking and savings accounts. The ninth prompt is effective for doing a quick sweep of your accounts to see if there are any anomalies or accidental double charges that have popped up across your linked accounts.

The tenth and final prompt is efficient since it can bring up any stored concert tickets on your Google Wallet while instantly accessing your local transit pass before you use any public transportation to get to your destination.

I’m surprised it took this long for Google to connect its Wallet tool to Gemini, especially since its competitor ChatGPT offers a similar financial tool already.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, it has finally arrived and sticks out as another useful way to utilize AI to give you a clearer picture of your spending habits so you can make more informed decisions about how to save & spend your money. And besides that, it can bring up any other information you need about your linked accounts to make subscription cancellations or whatever other actions you may need to take.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last week saw a truly epic outage to Microsoft 365, with a huge number of customers unable to send and receive emails. The company has now admitted that at the worst point, more than 80% of its servers were unresponsive.

Microsoft has now explained what went wrong, stating that the mistake that led to the failure was actually made all the way back in July without being detected ….

In a recent development, the tech giant said at the time that it was a technical issue and not a cyber attack, and that it was working hard to fix the problem, admitting that it was taking longer than expected. Microsoft also denied that it was related to the thousands of layoffs revealed the previous month.

Customers were understandably unimpressed at the scale of the outage and the time taken to fix it, although meme creators were having fun.

Sorry but you have to be change the name now. Thems the rules pic.twitter.com/5UttZ8nt9f.

It certainly points out that when you base your business on cloud services, you also take the risk that comes with that.

Platform head Charles Lamanna admitted the severity of the problem.

In a recent development, in less than two hours, the previously unknown defect was encountered across our fleet and rendered them unresponsive. At its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.

He remarked it resulted from a combination of two issues. The manufacturer maintains two independent network gateway systems, one of which failed, meaning that the remaining gateway took the full load. That wouldn’t have been a problem on its own, Microsoft stating that each one has enough capacity to handle all traffic. However, a mistake made back in July led to a cascading failure.

A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable. This defect was the result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers […].

According to recent reports, the initial change in behavior first started deployment in July of this year. The update went through safe deployment and saturated globally over several weeks, during which time no problems were observed. For more than three months, the change was deployed worldwide without impact. Our normal load testing did not detect the latent issue because the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs. The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.

In other words, the update wasn’t tested under the conditions in which it was most likely to fail.

While the company claims that the incident is unrelated to laying off staff and replacing them with AI systems, I find myself extremely skeptical. It seems inconceivable that a company of Microsoft’s size could make what appears to be a schoolboy error of this magnitude unless there were insufficient engineers working on the enhancement. Please share your own thoughts in the comments.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then indicates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Eight Crucial Router Settings You Should Check (or Change)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet.
  • Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network.
  • It has been revealed that some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet. This also makes it a highly valuable target for attackers and can leave your data vulnerable—especially if you simply plug your router in with its default settings unchanged. Whether your router is brand new or it's been a while since you audited your existing setup, these are the key settings to check and change right now.

Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network. WPA3 Personal is the newest standard and the most secure, so if it's available on your router, enable it. It's compatible with devices that support Wi-Fi 6. Some older devices may not work with WPA3, in which case the WPA2/WPA3 Transitional mixed mode is a good alternative. At minimum, set your router to WPA2 Personal (AES).

It has been revealed that some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard. (This is not the same as your network name or wifi password, which you set up later.) Default router passwords are searchable online, which leaves your router's admin settings open to anyone. Once you get into your dashboard for the first time, change the default credentials and enable two-factor authentication for your admin account if available.

Industry observers note that while some newer routers do have unique, device-specific defaults, it's a good idea to check this setting and ensure it's secure. If you're prompted to create custom admin credentials during the setup process, do it.

Recent findings suggest that your network name, or SSID, is how your network appears when you search for available wifi. By default, this may be the name of the router brand or a short string of characters, but you should choose something unique to your network. Make sure there's no identifying personal information, such as your name or house number. While you may be tempted to hide your network and obscure your SSID, this may actually make your information less secure, so keep this setting disabled. You can, however, add "_nomap" to the end of your network name, which prevents your router's physical coordinates from being mapped by location databases.

The password to access your network should also be unique and secure and should not include obvious personal information. One option to keep it memorable and easy to type is to create a passphrase using five to seven unrelated words that, combined, have at least 16 characters.

Industry observers note that two additional settings that leave your network vulnerable are Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and Universal Plug and Play (UPnP). The former lets users connect to your network with a PIN, which can be vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The latter allows smart devices to easily connect to your network—but this also allows malware to spread more readily. You may need to have UPnP on in order to connect devices initially but should disable it afterward.

Any easy win for your network security is segmenting traffic to different networks, so if one is compromised, the data on the others remain unaffected. Many wifi routers have a "guest mode," which creates a separate SSID and password that you can share with visitors instead of giving them your primary network credentials. You can also set up a separate network for all of your smart home and IoT devices so exploitable vulnerabilities in these devices don't put your computers, phones, and other connected devices at risk too.

According to recent reports, routers run a type of software—called firmware—just like any other device. Firmware controls the router's core functions and is not immune to vulnerabilities, which can be exploited by bad actors. And, just like other types of software, manufacturers occasionally push updates to patch these flaws. Check your router's dashboard to see if automatic updates are toggled on. Some devices require an opt-in for auto updates during setup, so you should enable them if they are off. Some routers may even require manual updates—in this case, set a monthly or quarterly (at minimum) calendar reminder to check for patches.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't.
  • Sources indicate that apple is presently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • According to recent reports, with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Sources indicate that apple is presently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other new features. But for users of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

According to recent reports, with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first new iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software update can introduce new hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

Recent findings suggest that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Industry observers note that apple made a big deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That noted, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some users may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the latest option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

To celebrate 25 years of Xbox, Microsoft has rolled out Xbox Playback. Similar to Spotify Wrapped, the feature pulls together a highlight reel of your gaming history, including your very first game, total hours played, top years, and longest play streak.

Whether you have been playing since the original Xbox era or jumped in more recently, checking your stats only takes a minute on either your console or a web browser, provided you know where to look and meet a few quick eligibility rules before the feature disappears at the end of the year.

Industry observers note that before checking your stats, keep a few rules in mind. To unlock a recap, your profile needs at least 1 Gamerscore, 1 achievement, and 1 minute of qualifying gameplay — plus at least 1 minute of gameplay on that console if you want to watch it directly on your Xbox dashboard.

It is a bit disappointing that Microsoft has limited the rollout to just 15 countries, especially for longtime players outside those regions hoping to celebrate the 25-year milestone.

Xbox Playback is only live through December 31, 2026, across Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Mexico, Poland, South Africa, Spain, the UK, and the US.

To launch the recap from your console, power on your Xbox, select your profile, and look for the Xbox Playback tile directly on your main home dashboard.

It has been revealed that if it does not appear immediately at the top, return to the home screen and scroll down to the Xbox 25 Years section to select Playback from there. You can also press the Xbox button on your controller, head down to the Store, and search for Xbox to find and launch the Playback tab.

If you are away from your console, you can watch your recap on a phone or computer by heading to the Official Xbox Playback Page.

Simply sign in with the Microsoft account linked to your Xbox profile, then press Play to watch your personalized 25-year gaming story, complete with your first game, total hours played, top years, and longest streak.

‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Review: Is Time Finally Running Out For The Dystopic Game Show Franchise?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that not so long ago, the old it’s-funny-because-it’s-true joke about soap operas was that people in soap operas never seemed to watch soap operas.
  • Sources indicate that aha, you might say.
  • In a recent development, it begins in District 12 in almost Hillbilly Elegy levels of poverty-porn, with the first of several irrelevant chapter headings: “The Birthday.” As we’ve already gathered, it is the 16th birthday of Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), and, once again, the reaping is the dark shadow that falls across his special day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that not so long ago, the old it’s-funny-because-it’s-true joke about soap operas was that people in soap operas never seemed to watch soap operas. But now that reality demonstrates have all but taken over that space, the function of soaps has evaporated almost entirely, while “unscripted TV” has absorbed all of its clichés. When it first appeared in 2012, The Hunger Games seemed fresh and even satirical; now, though, it just feels tired, and this sixth lackluster offering raises only one serious question: Hasn’t anyone forced to take part in a violent dystopic game show ever seen a violent dystopic game show before?

Sources indicate that aha, you might say. This is a prequel, taking place a full 24 years before the original. True, the citizens of Panem have only had to put up with 49 editions of the Hunger Games thus far, but, leaving aside the ancient art of combat-for-entertainment explored in both Gladiator movies, in our world the idea of films pitting humans against humans has been around since 1932’s The Most Dangerous Game — and we’ve seen it all before, even if they haven’t. True, the target audience for this wasn’t alive for Logan’s Run (1976), or The Running Man (1987), and would have certainly missed Bong Joon Ho’s little-seen Snowpiercer (2013). But most would have been around for Edgar Wright’s recent Running Man remake, which this film most closely resembles. Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, it begins in District 12 in almost Hillbilly Elegy levels of poverty-porn, with the first of several irrelevant chapter headings: “The Birthday.” As we’ve already gathered, it is the 16th birthday of Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), and, once again, the reaping is the dark shadow that falls across his special day. When one of the “tributes” tries to do a runner (and is killed in the process), Haymitch is forced to take his place, along with local girls Maysilee Donner (McKenna Grace, who also plays her twin sister Merrilee) and Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), plus unpopular oddsmaker Wyatt Callow (Ben Wang).

RELATED: Everything We Know About The ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Movie So Far.

In a recent development, they are all duly whisked off to the Capitol, where Haymitch is given a makeover by the lascivious fashionista Effie Trinket (Elle Fanning) and built up as the show’s bad boy by overacting show host Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin) — who, admittedly, does have some good one-liners (“Look alive, children, while you still can!”). But the tributes’ first outing during the opening parade goes horribly wrong when Louella is killed in a chariot crash, not that you’d notice much difference. She is rapidly replaced by a lookalike, the equally inconsequential Lou Lou, but not before Haymitch upsets the vindictive, all-seeing, all-powerful President Coriolanus Snow (Ralph Fiennes), who sadistically does… Well, nothing at all, or at least not just yet. Just you wait, Haymitch Abernathy!!!!

RELATED: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Album Boasts 29 Songs.

As he trains for the games and prepares to enter The Arena, Haymitch gets involved in a fiendish plot to sabotage the whole enterprise, something that involves a young newbie called Ampert and his father Beetee, who is being cruelly forced to mentor his son before watching his untimely death. “The Arena is a killing machine, but all machines can be broken,” says Beetee, demonstrating this epochal moment by using a potato to turn a little fairy light on. In the meantime, Haymitch has found an unlikely potential ally in cameraman Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons), who drops heavy hints that he is playing both ends against the middle and offers to turn a blind eye to the blueprint.

Playing Haymitch as nothing at all like the adult Woody Harrelson he will later grow up into, Zada has a naïve, doe-eyed charm that helps suspend disbelief for at least two hours of the film’s increasingly tedious running time. That indicates a lot considering The Arena itself is quite ridiculously unscary, with its prospect of poisonous plants, electric butterflies and man-eating beavers — or maybe rats, it was hard to tell even in Imax — about as terrifying as being mauled to death by The Wonderful World of Disney. Worse, though, there is no sense of peril at all this time, even when Snow finally gets round to getting his drawn-out revenge: The Hunger Games has reached its High School Musical moment where everyone gets a participation prize, and any significant death is obviously just an unfortunate accident. The cast of the original film appear briefly at the end; one can’t shake the feeling that it’s to pay their last respects.

Title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the ReapingDistributor: LionsgateRelease date: November 20, 2026Director: Francis LawrenceScreenwriters: Billy Ray, Michael LesslieCast: Joseph Zada, McKenna Grace, Ben Wang, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Glenn Close, Billy Porter, Whitney PeakRating: PG-13Running time: 2 hrs 38 mins.

U.S. data centers emit as much CO2 as all of Denmark, Harvard study finds

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, every time you ask ChatGPT a question, generate an image with Gemini, or have Claude help write an email, a data center somewhere is doing the work.
  • Recent findings suggest that A upcoming Harvard-led study published in Nature Sustainability finds that 403 of the largest U.S.
  • That's an estimated 82 terawatt-hours of electricity in a single year, enough to power nearly 7 million American homes for a year, according to an Associated Press report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every time you ask ChatGPT a question, generate an image with Gemini, or have Claude help write an email, a data center somewhere is doing the work. Most of us never think about what it takes to keep those servers running, but new research suggests America's AI infrastructure already has an enormous environmental cost.

Recent findings suggest that A upcoming Harvard-led study published in Nature Sustainability finds that 403 of the largest U.S. data centers consumed about 1.8% of the country's total electricity between May 2024 and April 2025.

That's an estimated 82 terawatt-hours of electricity in a single year, enough to power nearly 7 million American homes for a year, according to an Associated Press report.

And electricity consumption is only part of the problem. Researchers estimate the facilities produced 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, roughly equivalent to Denmark's annual emissions.

Companies are racing to build more infrastructure to support increasingly powerful AI models, but questions remain over what the technology's rapid growth means for the environment and the people living near the facilities powering it.

Using satellite imagery, facility information and federal electricity-generation data, the team estimated how much power each location consumed and the resulting carbon emissions.

Approximately 54% of the electricity attributed to the data centers came from fossil-fuel generation, including 38% from natural gas and 15% from coal.

The estimated emissions were also two to three times higher than an earlier assessment of hyperscale data-center emissions in 2018. The study's measurements ended in April 2025, which means they don't even account for the additional data centers built or expanded over the past year and a half.

As AI companies release more capable models and add features such as image generation, video creation and autonomous agents, demand for computing infrastructure continues to grow.

However, the study doesn't tell us exactly how much electricity one ChatGPT conversation consumes, or whether Gemini uses more power than Claude.

In a recent development, the researchers couldn't distinguish between electricity used for AI-specific workloads and traditional cloud-computing operations. That means the findings shouldn't be interpreted as emissions caused exclusively by generative AI.

Industry observers note that still, they provide a revealing look at the infrastructure supporting the AI services millions of people are adopting. And unlike the electricity consumed by a household appliance, the environmental impact of an AI request isn't necessarily visible to the person using the technology.

Power plants that burn fossil fuels release pollutants that can affect air quality and human health.

It has been revealed that the Harvard researchers pointed to fine particulate matter, nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide as pollutants associated with fossil-fuel generation. Exposure to these pollutants is linked to respiratory and cardiovascular problems.

That means communities located near power plants could experience environmental consequences from data centers operating miles away.

The researchers did not directly measure those health effects, but they identified the problem as an important area for future investigation.

Location also makes a difference. The study found that Virginia, Oregon, Ohio, and Iowa accounted for more than half of the electricity consumption across the facilities examined.

Some data centers also operate in regions where electricity generation is substantially more carbon-intensive than the national average.

Using cleaner electricity, improving hardware efficiency and making data-center energy consumption more transparent could all help reduce the industry's environmental footprint.

But there's a fundamental challenge. As AI becomes faster, cheaper and more widely available, more people and businesses are finding reasons to use it.

Industry observers note that for consumers, the takeaway is that AI may feel effortless, but the infrastructure behind it is anything but. And as the technology becomes part of everyday life, the question is how much energy we're willing to use to make it happen.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Political ad spending on the 2025-26 election cycle topped more than $12 billion, a particular boon to broadcasters, streamers and digital outlets.
  • The figures for the 2025-26 cycle are from a new report from analysis firm AdImpact.
  • Per the firm, this was the first midterm election to outspend a presidential cycle, with spending 8% above 2024, when spending was $11.2 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Political ad spending on the 2025-26 election cycle topped more than $12 billion, a particular boon to broadcasters, streamers and digital outlets.

The figures for the 2025-26 cycle are from a new report from analysis firm AdImpact.

Per the firm, this was the first midterm election to outspend a presidential cycle, with spending 8% above 2024, when spending was $11.2 billion. It also was 35% about the 2022 midterm and three times the 2018 cycle.

In a recent development, broadcast saw $5.85 billion in political ad revenue, up 9% from 2024, while its share actually grew from 48% to 49%. Streaming, or connected TV, grew by 14% to $2.66 billion and digital rose by 11% to $1.91 billion. Spending on cable declined by 7%, radio dropped by 13% and satellite fell by 7%. Spending doesn’t guarantee wins: Republicans outspent Democrats, $5.51 billion to $5.11 billion, according to AdImpact. GOP spending rose by 27% while Democrats saw their spending fall by 4% compared to 2024. Per The Latest York Times, Elon Musk spent $474 million during the cycle, albeit not all of that figure was for advertising. Watch on Deadline.

All that stated, Republicans saw their biggest trouncing since 1974, with Democrats winning back control of the two chambers of Congress, among other gains.

October spending was $4.10 billion, a monthly record, and even earlier months saw huge sums. Almost $700 million was spent on ads in May, as primaries were in full swing, and the off year elections in 2025 saw $1.86 billion spent. That was a 32% growth over 2023.

Records were broken in spending on Senate races, with $3.39 billion, the House, with $2.44 billion and gubernatorial races, at $2.61 billion.

Recent findings suggest that A Supreme Court decision allowed for coordinated buys by candidates and party committees, and that reached a record $258 million from September 1 through Election Day, up 62% from 2024. The cycle continued to see huge spending by SuperPACs, which, unlike official committees, do not receive the lowest unit charge for their ad buys.
