📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The ongoing earnings season, investor concerns about the durability of AI demand and spending, and geopolitical risks are key factors that have been contributing to stock market volatility in recent trading sessions.

In this scenario, investors seeking steady income can consider adding dividend stocks to their portfolios. Recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help them pick attractive dividend stocks that are backed by solid cash flows to support consistent payments.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Oil and gas exploration and production firm ConocoPhillips is this week's first dividend pick. With a dividend of 84 cents per share (annualized dividend of $3.36 per share), COP offers a dividend yield of 3%. The company is scheduled to announce its second-quarter results on Aug. 6.

Ahead of second-quarter results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin reiterated a buy rating on COP stock with a price target of $183. Despite the pressure on oil prices from an increase in OPEC production quota, the analyst finds ConocoPhillips and Shell stocks appealing as the earnings season approaches. He cited their operational visibility and resilience as factors backing their appeal.

The 5-star analyst expects ConocoPhillips to meet its production guidance of 2.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day at the mid-point. He expects lower Waha natural gas prices in the Permian Basin to be offset by stronger Brent crude premiums. Margolin expects capital expenditure to remain within COP's prior guided range of $12.2 billion annualized, with no significant impact on spending on the Northfield East project in Qatar despite the Strait of Hormuz disruption.

Overall, Margolin expects COP to generate about $3.5 billion in free cash flow (before working capital) and earnings per share of $2.94. He expects continued strength in COP's free cash flow and regular dividend growth through the completion of the Willow project in 2028/2029. Prior to the Willow project coming online, the analyst expects free cash flow to grow by about $2 billion in 2027 and 2028, assuming Brent crude averages around $60 per barrel.

"COP's track record of capital efficiency and strong Permian well productivity underpins its ability to pursue long-cycle developments," remarked Margolin.

In a recent development, margolin ranks No. 457 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 70% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.3%. See ConocoPhillips Financials on TipRanks.

Sources indicate that energy Transfer is a limited partnership that operates 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. With a quarterly cash distribution of 33.75 cents per common unit ($1.35 per unit on an annualized basis), ET offers a yield of 6.8%.

Heading into Energy Transfer's Q2 earnings on Aug. 4, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith reaffirmed a buy rating on ET stock with a price target of $23. The analyst noted that his adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization estimate of $4.46 billion is 1% below the Street's consensus of $4.49 billion.

It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst noted that Energy Transfer has slightly outperformed Enterprise Products Partners recently. However, it still trades at a relative discount of 19% compared to EPD, which is below its historical discount range of 17%-20%. Smith believes that ET stock could be re-rated higher if the organization provides a clearer long-term strategy for natural gas growth.

Furthermore, Smith expects the current energy market to support a stronger outlook for natural gas liquids and crude oil. "The current energy macro backdrop positions ET to benefit in all three commodities," stated the analyst.

He expects Energy Transfer's adjusted EBITDA to grow at a 4.8% compound annual growth rate in 2027-2030, which is 1%-3% above Wall Street's expectations. In fact, Smith sees the possibility of additional upside if ET reveals more natural gas projects. He added that investors will await details on final investment decisions on newly introduced natural gas projects and any clues about additional projects in the pipeline. The analyst noted that ET has revealed new gas projects consistently in recent quarters.

Smith ranks No. 550 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.4%. See Energy Transfer Statistics on TipRanks.

Finally, let's look at energy giant Chevron, which is scheduled to announce its second-quarter results on July 31. Last month, the company paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12, CVX offers a dividend yield of 3.92%.

Ahead of Q2 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on Chevron stock and lowered his price target to $216 from $236. Byrne expects the firm to report adjusted EPS of about $5.86 per share, nearly 9% above the Street's expectations.

In a recent development, the 5-star analyst highlighted that the challenges seen in Chevron's upstream business in the first quarter due to the disruption at the Tengizchevroil joint venture in Kazakhstan, Storm Fern downtime, and the Middle East conflict have largely been resolved. Consequently, Byrne expects production to recover in the second quarter to about 4,033 mboepd. He expects the upstream business to generate adjusted earnings of about $8.1 billion in Q2 2026.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Byrne expects Chevron to generate downstream adjusted earnings of about $4.4 billion in Q2, with strength in both domestic and international markets. The downstream business benefited from higher crack spreads and strong refining performance.

Additionally, the analyst expects Chevron to generate $18.2 billion in cash flow from operations (before working capital changes), driven by stronger earnings and about $2.2 billion in dividends from affiliated companies. Unlike the first quarter, Chevron is not expected to make a TCO loan repayment in Q2, providing an additional boost to cash flow.

10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth.
  • The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.
  • In a recent development, an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?).

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

In a recent development, an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

The Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

Sources indicate that one of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

Industry observers note that if you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

If you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it massive and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for new planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

It has been revealed that want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

If you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous upcoming reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

Recent findings suggest that if you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend notes a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there’s one upgrade I’m looking forward to seeing most on the iPhone 20 Pro, it’s the camera. The latest rumor has me excited because Apple is reportedly introducing a far more advanced imaging sensor, which could deliver dramatic improvements.

Sources indicate that although the iPhone 18 Pro Max is still one of the best camera phones around today, I was somewhat disappointed to find minimal upgrades in my iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. iPhone 17 Pro Max face-off. In almost every snapshot, the differences between them were nearly indistinguishable.

Recent findings suggest that that’s why all eyes will be on Apple’s next flagship release. According to Weibo leaker Ice Universe, the iPhone 20 Pro could feature a main camera sensor with logic circuitry manufactured on a new 17-nanometer process. Even though this doesn’t directly mean the sensor itself will be physically larger, a more advanced logic layer gives the camera the capacity to deliver faster readout speeds, handle more complex image processing, and consume less power.

Here’s what I think that could mean in practice:.

According to recent reports, most people don’t realize all the complex actions that go on behind the scenes the moment they tap the shutter button. The phone isn’t just capturing a single frame — it’s taking a rapid series of shots and processing them together to deliver one final image.

By introducing a more advanced image sensor that processes data faster, Apple could dramatically improve the iPhone 20 Pro’s dynamic range performance. Think about tricky, high-contrast lighting scenes where bright highlights compete with deep shadows. With a faster readout speed, the sensor could capture and merge exposures more effectively to balance those challenging areas.

Sources indicate that instead of leaving hotspots blown out by harsh light, the iPhone 20 Pro could better preserve detail in the highlights — all while lifting the shadows. You can see some of examples I'm referring to in the gallery above.

It has been revealed that apple has already made strides in this next area, but a more advanced image sensor could push things even further. I’m referring to zero shutter lag and reduced rolling shutter distortion when capturing fast-moving subjects. If you’ve ever tried photographing someone playing sports, you’re probably familiar with how easily those frames can come out blurry or out of focus.

Frenetic movement can make it tough to freeze a moment cleanly, so an image sensor with faster readout speeds would be much better equipped to handle the action. Just look at the side-by-side shots above of someone riding an electric scooter.

I shoot a ton of videos and know firsthand how quickly a phone can feel toasty whenever I record for more than a couple of minutes. If you really want to see how warm it gets, try shooting continuously for 10 minutes or longer.

In a recent development, sustained capture like that demands serious processing power, which swiftly leads to heat buildup. With a more power-efficient sensor, the iPhone 20 Pro could be better equipped to handle longer ProRes recording sessions without pausing due to overheating.

In a recent development, the iPhone 20 Pro is still a long way away, but this 17nm sensor rumor could become much more exciting if the sensor size itself increases. Apple certainly delighted us with a mechanical variable aperture main camera on the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, yet a physically larger sensor would be a compelling reason to upgrade to the iPhone 20 Pro.

This wouldn’t just improve its light-gathering abilities, but would also help boost detail, sharpness, and definition. If these leaks pan out, next year's anniversary iPhone could deliver the biggest leap in iPhone photography we've seen in years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When cinematographer Katelin Arizmendi boarded Bassam Tariq’s genre-defying sophomore feature film Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, the pair were both new to the action genre and a key challenge they faced during the 30-day shoot was making sure action sequences didn’t drown out the emotional core of the film.

“We knew that we were making a movie with action, but we knew that we weren’t making an action movie,” Arizmendi tells Deadline during the ToruńCamerimage Film Festival.

The action drama stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devout Muslim contract killer and grieving widower in Houston whose life is upended when he must balance raising his three young children – including a newborn daughter in urgent need of breast milk – while pulled into a violent conflict with a religious extremist group. Related Stories Festivals 'Fatherland' Takes Top Prize At ToruńCamerimage; 'Wild Horse Nine' Wins Audience Award News 'Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother' Star Mahershala Ali Says It Can Be "Dangerous That People End Up Believing Their Own Righteousness" -- Contenders L.A.

Recent findings suggest that “We knew that the visual language needed to be built off of the journey of the characters and the emotion and the perspective of Latif first,” says Arizmendi. “Both of us were fresh to action. Bassam had almost shot Blade and then I did second unit on Dune, so I had shot action, but I hadn’t ever been the main DP to design action films and action sequences. So, it was trying to marry the two so that the action felt exciting and it felt studio level and theatrical but that it didn’t feel like a different movie, because really the core of the story is this family and this man’s journey and his spiritual journey and his struggles of trying to step up as a father while dealing with the loss of his love and the mother of his three children. There were so many things that were driving the visual language.” Watch on Deadline.

Early conversations, she states, involved making sure to spotlight Latif’s teenage daughter Fatiha (played by Adia) because of the impact she had on Latif throughout the story.

“I wanted her to visually hold as much weight in each frame because she’s always standing up to him and shining a light back on him to reflect himself and she challenges him,” she says. “So, I wanted her to have a strong presence.”.

Key fight sequences, she says, were initially challenging. “I knew how I didn’t want them to look almost more than I knew how I wanted them to look at first,” she says.

“I knew I didn’t want them to go handheld, and I knew I wanted the rest of the film to have much more calm, precise camera movements so I didn’t want the action to go handheld. We talked about that with the stunt coordinator very early on. I knew that we also needed to keep in tune with the emotion of each fight sequence, so it wasn’t like there was no purpose to any of it. We needed to stay grounded in where Latif’s emotional journey was throughout each fight.”.

Arizmendi also points to the significance of the high angle shots, which feature throughout the film: “I wanted to play with these high angles as him being judged by a higher power and so those either come before or after the violence.”.

The Amazon/MGM Studios film has a very rich and textured color palate, something that Arizmendi notes was born after she attended a prayer service at a mosque, which gave her a sense of how deep the colors needed to feel on screen.

According to recent reports, “It started there with knowing how rich and saturated we wanted the film to look as well and then in contrast, the Christians are wearing white and camouflage and are brightly lit,” she states. “We also had discussions about prayer times in Islam, which I didn’t know so much and that was really vital because it dictates where the sun is. We talked about that really early on and I put that into my lookbook as well because it needed to be really honest.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After tackling such real-life ghouls as Ed Gein and Jeffrey Dahmer, Netflix’s “Monster” anthology finally got to its first female perpetrator in the form of the infamous Lizzie Borden, the young American woman who was tried and acquitted of the gruesome 1892 axe murders of her father and stepmother in Fall River, Massachusetts.

All eight episodes of “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story” dropped on the streaming service back in September, with Ella Beatty (Feud: Capote vs. The Swans) leading the cast as Lizzie. (The star-studded ensemble also included Vicky Krieps, Charlie Hunnam, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Sarah Paulson, Jessica Barden and Joey Pollari.) And it was an instant hit with Netflix viewers, knocking fellow buzzy newcomer “Crew Girl” off the top spot of the streamer’s charts. Now that the dust has settled, you might be looking for a follow-up.

So, if it's more Lizzie Borden you want, we’ve got it: Here are three films and series that dig into the true-crime story.

In this 2018 biographical thriller from Craig William Macneill, Chloë Sevigny is our titular protagonist, a thirtysomething spinster and social outcast trapped under the strict, suffocating control of her austere father Andrew (Jamey Sheridan) and stepmother Abby (Fiona Shaw). Lizzie finds an unexpected kindred spirit in the form of the Borden family’s young Irish maid Bridget Sullivan (Kristen Stewart), a bond that turns romantic and, later, deadly, as the women seemingly carry out the killings of Lizzie’s parents.

Though the major-screen take on Borden’s story only received a 66% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, critics complimented Sevigny’s portrayal of the real-life woman: “Ms. Sevigny's intelligence and formidable control keep the melodrama grounded,” wrote Jeannette Catsoulis of The New York Times. “Her empathy for Borden, whose fragile constitution belies a searing will, is palpable, as is the sense of inescapable peril surrounding the two female leads.".

Rent or buy “Lizzie” on Prime Video now.

Christina Ricci first took on the complicated role of Lizzie Borden in the 2014 TV movie "Lizzie Borden Took an Ax,” which delves into the crimes for which Lizzie was tried.

But this follow-up limited series for Lifetime follows Borden in the months after her controversial acquittal in the murders of her father and stepmother, with Lizzie and her older sister Emma (Clea DuVall) shunned from society and trying to make a new life for themselves in Fall River, Massachusetts. Meanwhile, Pinkerton detective Charlie Siringo (Cole Hauser) arrives in town to investigate Lizzie’s case for himself, right as even more bodies start popping up.

Ricci earned a SAG nomination for her performance here: The actress “was born to play a 19th-century ax murderer, as it turns out,” wrote Jane Borden for Vanity Fair, calling the series "playful, wicked brain candy.”.

Stream “The Lizzie Borden Chronicles” on Prime Video now.

And for something a little different, this 2022 horror-thriller stars Odessa A'zion as Tara Haldon, a Fall River, MA high schooler who's the descendant of the notorious axe murderer Lizzie Borden.

Recent findings suggest that believing her bloodline to be cursed, the tormented teen struggles with sinister visions, dark impulses, and deep anxieties, which certainly don’t lessen when several townspeople are discovered murdered. Soon, Tara isn’t just questioning her own sanity but her own family’s darkest secrets. Leslie Bibb and Dermot Mulroney play Tara’s parents; Lizzie Broadway, Kenneisha Thompson and Todd Jenkins also feature.

Stream “The Inhabitant” on Tubi now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 beta 2 is now available, and Apple is adding the ability for users to unlock higher usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI via iCloud+. Here’s everything you need to know.

From the start, Apple has said that some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features have usage limits because “they rely on powerful server models.” The company previously outlined that increased access would be available across most iCloud+ subscription intends, and now we have the full details on how this will work.

Apple says the fresh system applies to several categories of Apple Intelligence features, including:.

In a recent development, the usage limits are per device, not per account. This means your iPhone, iPad, and Mac each have separate allowances. Apple isn’t disclosing specific limit numbers. Instead, it says that limits can vary based on the feature, request complexity, system demand, and more.

As you near your limit, you’ll see an alert within whichever feature you’re using. For example, if you are using Image Playground, a message will appear telling you that you’ve almost hit your usage limit for the day. Once you hit the limit, you’ll be prompted to wait for it to reset or upgrade your iCloud+ blueprint.

If you hit your limit, basic Siri requests will still work. This includes things like setting timers and alarms. Requests that require Siri to understand personal context and perform more complex, multi-step actions, however, are subject to the limits.

For example, asking Siri to find the details of an upcoming dinner reservation in your email and add them to your calendar would count toward your daily limit.

Additionally, each device uses its own standard daily usage limit first. After that, it can tap into the additional capacity included with an eligible iCloud+ subscription:.

Sources indicate that the usage unlocked by iCloud+ is shared across all devices signed in to your Apple Account, as well as family members sharing your iCloud+ strategy. The shared usage is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

All limits will reset daily at the same time, and limits don’t roll over. In most cases, limits reset around midnight in your current time zone.

Apple has published a support document with more details.

Breaking: macOS 27.3 includes new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and more

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last month, Apple unveiled its aims to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access amid the rise of “increasingly capable and autonomous” AI agents.

With today’s new macOS 27.3 beta, Apple is implementing several changes as part of this.

In a post on its developer website last month, Apple said some developers are “using Full Disk Access in ways that could put customers at risk, exposing everything on their systems.” As such, it said that it would “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

In macOS 27.2, “Device Control and Data Access” is a unified toggle in System Settings, where Apple says that apps with that level of access can “view and send email, edit contacts and photos, monitor your keyboard, track websites, record your screen, control any app on your Mac, and more.”.

In macOS 27.3, Apple is splitting “Device Control and Data Access” into two categories:.

For the latter, people will be able to specify which apps an automation tool can access rather than granting it unrestricted control. For instance, you could give an app access to the Mail app, but not Messages.

macOS 27.3 also adds an option for users to require an app to request permission every time it needs access, rather than granting it access indefinitely.

Sources indicate that apple is also introducing a newly introduced menu bar indicator that will provide additional transparency when an app is controlling another app with System and App Protection Override. This is designed to let users know when an automation tool is interacting with apps and information in the background.

Crucially, Apple isn’t removing the ability to give an app Full Disk Access. If you deem it necessary, you can still give an app Full Disk Access. However, Apple is redesigning the approval process to make the implications of that decision more obvious.

macOS 27.3 will display a more detailed explanation about the protections being bypassed and the types of personal information that could be exposed.

According to recent reports, people can also choose to grant an app access to specific folders instead of their entire Mac. For example, an app that only needs to work with files in a particular folder won’t get unrestricted access to everything else.

According to recent reports, any app you’ve already given Full Disk Access will still have that access. Previously granted permissions will remain in effect, and those apps will continue functioning as they do today without any approval required.

Apple has published a new support document detailing the Full Disk Access updates.

macOS 27.3 now warns you before giving an app full disk accessThat warning prompt is pretty scary! pic.twitter.com/J2qCKVWJRx.

Apple claims the underlying APIs aren’t changing, but developers will need to patch their apps to account for situations where people grant limited access rather than unrestricted permissions.

In a recent development, finally, Apple claims developers of backup apps and assistive technologies can request entitlements that allow them to maintain the same experience for upcoming installations as before macOS 27.3. Apple has already identified popular apps that rely on these permissions, and those apps will continue working as expected without requiring an entitlement.

Developers can read more on Apple’s Developer website.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In today’s iOS 27.3 beta release, Apple is introducing two changes for iPhone Duo people.
  • Apple is also adding an option to have your iPhone Duo lock when you close it.
  • You can enable the fresh option to unlock your iPhone Duo with the front camera in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode, after updating to iOS 27.3.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In today’s iOS 27.3 beta release, Apple is introducing two changes for iPhone Duo people. Most notably, it adds a new face recognition option that lets you unlock your iPhone Duo by looking at it.

Apple is also adding an option to have your iPhone Duo lock when you close it.

You can enable the fresh option to unlock your iPhone Duo with the front camera in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode, after updating to iOS 27.3. When enabled, your iPhone Duo will unlock after recognizing your face.

In the Settings app, Apple indicates:.

It has been revealed that use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

Industry observers note that this isn’t Face ID. This new option on iPhone Duo uses the front camera on the outer iPhone Duo display to recognize your face. The iPhone Duo doesn’t have the hardware needed for Face ID.

Because this isn’t as secure as Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode, Apple has implemented a few guardrails. First, the setting only works to unlock your iPhone Duo. To use Apple Pay, access your passwords, unlock apps, and do other things that require authentication, you’ll have to use Touch ID or enter your passcode.

In a recent development, this face recognition feature also has a time-based limitation. After 45 minutes of inactivity, you have to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. That is, if you go 45 minutes without unlocking your iPhone Duo, the facial recognition feature is disabled until you enter your passcode or use Touch ID.

Finally, this new feature also doesn’t work when using the iPhone Duo unfolded. When unfolded, you still have to use Touch ID or your passcode to unlock the device.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds an option to lock your iPhone Duo when you close it. You can enable this in Settings, under Display & Brightness. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold, rather than transition from the inner display to the outer display.

Many iPhone Duo users (myself included) have noted Apple should do this. Personally, I’ve been using a shortcut to mimic this behavior, but I’m glad to see that Apple has listened to user feedback and added a default setting for it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Will Packer is launching a microdrama studio, with NBCUniversal (NBCU) among the backers.

June is being as an “entertainment and content” business that will develop, produce, finance and acquire original scripted microdramas designed for Black audiences. Culturally-relevant storytelling for mobile users will be the focus.

Sherrese Clarke’s HarbourView Equity Partners and NBCUniversal are investing in June, and provide resources and strategic support. Will Packer will serve as CEO and his son, Dom Packer, will serve as President, overseeing strategy, operations and growth. Related Stories News TikTok Creator Videos Coming To Disney+ In December As Hulu Integration Takes Full Effect News French Microdrama App Shortstory Opens $1.1M Funding Round.

This is the latest example of a Hollywood studio backing a vertical video venture, with Fox Entertainment Group owning a stake in Ukraine-based Holywater and influential independent players launching their own businesses, as the U.S. microdrama boom deepens. Watch on Deadline.

Will Packer has produced movies with a combined gross of over $1B. He’s worked with Universal Pictures several times on the likes of Girls Trip, Night School and the Ride Along franchise, as well as exec-producing Universal Television’s Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist, theb Peacock’s original series.

“Will has a seasoned instinct for stories that resonate with audiences and June is an opportunity to pair that creative vision with a format built for how viewers are engaging today,” stated Liz Jenkins, Chief Business Officer, NBCUniversal Entertainment.

Industry observers note that “Our strategy isn’t about chasing a format, we always start in the same place: with the story, the storyteller and the audience. This is exactly the kind of creator-first partnership we want to build, working with storytellers to evolve thoughtfully, learn quickly, and aim to define the future of mobile-native storytelling.”.

“I’ve always believed in telling authentic stories that meet audiences where they are, and with June, we’re building a home for those stories alongside Sherrese Clarke, her expert team at HarbourView and my longtime trusted partners at NBCUniversal,” said Will Packer.

It has been revealed that “The name captures the warmth and romance of summer and celebrates Black freedom and culture through Juneteenth and Black Music Month. That spirit of joy, connection and pride is at the heart of what we’re creating.”.

Industry observers note that “Vertical entertainment offers an intimacy and immediacy that can make culturally resonant storytelling especially powerful,” said Clarke, founder and CEO of HarbourView, which will primarily. “Will and Dom’s vision for June puts the experiences and perspectives of an audience that has helped shape music, entertainment, and culture around the world at the heart of this category, and HarbourView is proud to help bring it to life, empowering a studio that can create stories and connect them to the brands that want to reach this audience.”.

June’s first slate is being developed with Black women at its core, pairing the romance, heightened drama and cliffhangers common to microdramas with culturally-resonant storytelling that Will Packer’s film and television work includes.

June flagged several reports to back its launch, including a Pew Research Center survey that indicated 51% of Black adults in the U.S. use TikTok, compared with 37% of all U.S. adults, and a Nielsen report from 2025 that found Black adults spend more than 23 hours a week on smartphone apps and websites.

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (763 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Tomsguide ↗ Open Full Page

How to stop your floorboards creaking this winter — 5 top tips from an expert

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that winter is a time when we spend more time indoors.
  • I'd wrongly assumed that I was noticing it more because my little kids are growing up and making noticeably less noise (or arguably, at times, more).
  • Here's why your floorboards are creaking and an expert's top tips on how to stop it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that winter is a time when we spend more time indoors. It's also a time when you might start to notice some noises in your home that you may not have heard in the warmer months. And there's one noise in particular that's started to bother me – the squeaking and creaking of floorboards.

I'd wrongly assumed that I was noticing it more because my little kids are growing up and making noticeably less noise (or arguably, at times, more). But certainly at night I hear it – and it turns out there's a reason.

Here's why your floorboards are creaking and an expert's top tips on how to stop it.

Sources indicate that tony Reynolds, Managing Director at Supreme Merchants has worked in the builders' merchant industry for 15 years. So, he's pretty clued up on the workings of a home.

And for creaking floorboards in the colder months of the year, he reveals: "During winter, when the heating is on more frequently, indoor air can become much drier, causing wooden floorboards to lose some of their moisture.".

He adds: "As the timber dries, it can shrink slightly, creating small gaps between boards or around the fixings. When you walk across the floor, the boards can then rub against each other or the joists underneath, which is what causes that familiar creaking sound.".

Fortunately, you don't have to put up with the creaking floorboards in exchange for a warm home as Reynolds has shared his 5 top tips for silencing the woodwork, for good.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Recent findings suggest that when the cold weather hits, it can be tempting to turn your heating up to max, hoping to shock it into warming up your home. Reynolds says don't: "Turning the heating up dramatically can cause indoor conditions to fluctuate." Instead, he suggests doing it gradually so the timber can get used to it.

It has been revealed that while loose boards and gaps can be there all year round, the change in temperature will be sure to highlight them. So, if you notice certain spots keep creaking, you may need to stabilize and secure the floorboards.

If it's a gap, Reynolds warns: "Avoid filling them with unsuitable materials, as the wood may expand again when humidity rises.".

As mentioned, dry indoor air can be the cause of creaking floorboards. But lowering your heating levels isn't always necessary to combat it. Instead, Reynolds explains: "Maintaining a more consistent humidity level can help reduce excessive moisture changes in timber.".

For this, he recommends buying a humidifier if you've noticed the air in your home is particularly dry.

Sources indicate that this Levoit humidifier has a 4.2 liter capacity for major rooms, an easy top-fill, night light, aroma diffuser and can run for 42 hours. It's even easy to clean with a specialized detachable tray meaning you can empty and wipe it ready to move around your home where you're noticing dry air.

It's not just the floorboards themselves that can be loose; sometimes it's the nails and screws that are holding them in place. If you've noticed a particularly creaky and loose spot, Reynolds adds: "Appropriate flooring fixings can help reduce this movement.".

Recent findings suggest that finally, and hopefully unlikely, is keeping an eye out for any damp patches around your home. "If floorboards feel soft, appear discolored, or have developed a musty smell, investigate further," Reynolds explains. These can be signs of a more serious glitch that you don't want to ignore.

So, instead of just hopping over the creaking floorboards and hoping they'll go away, it's better to address the issue as soon as possible.

Sources indicate that fortunately, with these top tips, you'll be able to keep seasonal creaking to a minimum. "The important thing is to understand why the boards are moving rather than simply trying to silence the noise.".

YouTube creator Topper Guild is working with kids animation manufacturer Toonstar on an original animated series.

Industry observers note that “Animation is a medium I’ve always wanted to work in, but I didn’t think it was possible to maintain that same pace my fans expect, or retain the creative control I have with my live-action content,” he noted. “But Toonstar changed that. “Topper is the kind of creator who understands exactly what his generation wants,” said John Attanasio, co-founder and CEO of Toonstar. “Working with us, he can bring his unique storytelling style to animation and expand his reach with a show that feels like him and also has a path to becoming franchise IP.”.

WME represented Toonstar and Guild on the deal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when you open Apple’s Calendar app in iOS 27.3, the interface will look largely familiar to what was there before. But there are some key design changes that make the app better suited for one-handed use.

Most notably, the buttons for search and for adding a upcoming event have both been moved from the top of the screen to the bottom.

This is a welcome change for anyone who uses their iPhone one-handed a lot, as both key buttons were previously in the top-right corner. I normally use my iPhone in my left hand, so they were especially hard to reach before.

Additionally, Apple has moved the current month to the top-center of the screen and added the year too. Because the year is now always prominently visible, Apple removed it from the back button in the top-left.

Finally, the ‘Today’ button that takes you back to the current day has been changed to always show the actual date. So right now, it reads ‘Mon 16.’.

Sources indicate that you can reference the full side-by-side in the image above. Overall, these are relatively minor changes but they could make a big difference in everyday use.

Apple is rolling out the second developer beta of macOS 27.3 ahead of the official launch of the enhancement, which includes several notable additions. Here’s what’s coming.

Two weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27.3 developer beta 1, followed by the public beta a few days later, amid a slew of hardware releases that included fresh M6-powered iMacs and 14-inch MacBook Pro, and the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.

According to recent reports, and contrary to macOS 27.2, the latest upgrade is shaping up to be pretty significant. In addition to expanding Siri AI support to four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese, the system also expands Siri AI’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing people to perform more complex actions in apps like Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders.

macOS 27.3 beta 2 also introduces new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and you can read more about that here. This change comes in response to concerns about increasingly capable AI agents gaining broad access to users’ personal data and control over their Macs.

Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to create advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions, allowing the assistant to coordinate multistep actions across different apps.

It has been revealed that macOS 27.3 also introduces Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari, as well as native Live Activities support in the menu bar. Additionally, macOS 27.3 so far include native Markdown rendering in Quick Look, a new Pro Light screensaver, and additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through public iCloud links.

The build number for macOS 27.3 Golden Gate developer beta 2 is 26C5047e. We are digging through the system and will report back with what we find.

Recent findings suggest that in this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist stocks with robust growth opportunities. These experts conduct an in-depth analysis of all the macro and micro factors affecting a manufacturer, focusing on its long-term growth potential.

CrowdStrike Holdings is a cloud-native cybersecurity provider. The company recently announced an expanded partnership with Schwarz Digits to bring its Falcon platform to European enterprises.

After hosting several European investor meetings with the CrowdStrike CFO, Stifel analyst Adam Borg reiterated a buy rating on CRWD stock and increased his price target to $230 from $220.

The five-star analyst said that the meetings increased his confidence about CrowdStrike being an "vital, well-positioned cybersecurity platform vendor that is an AI beneficiary given its expansive portfolio, unique data set, and ability to both secure AI and use AI to improve security.".

Among the key takeaways, Borg noted that AI is driving a major shift in cybersecurity demand as it presents software vulnerabilities that can be exploited by less sophisticated hackers with capabilities that were once limited to government-backed hacking groups. This has led to companies making cybersecurity a top priority, driving customer interest in CrowdStrike's new AI Detection & Response solution and its broader security platform.

Industry observers note that borg added that AI-driven demand is expanding CrowdStrike's pipeline and supporting confidence in the firm's higher fiscal 2027 net new annual recurring revenue guidance issued last quarter. Overall, Borg believes that CrowdStrike has multiple growth drivers that can help maintain revenue growth in at least the high-teens and drive improved profitability in the years ahead.

Borg ranks No. 651 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 65% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See CrowdStrike Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Moving on to AST SpaceMobile, a tech giant building a global cellular broadband network in space. Recently, Piper Sandler analyst Alexander Potter initiated coverage of space-related stocks. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Siri AI expanded on what kinds of things you can ask Apple’s voice assistant in many ways, one area where the system took a step back was health data. Since Siri AI’s launch in iOS 27.0, the system has enforced guardrails that do not allow it to access data from the Health app, despite the older Siri Classic being able to do just that.

Sources indicate that however, it seems Apple is about to close the gap. In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, just released to developers today, consumers are now able to ask their iPhone about health data related questions and Siri AI will answer.

For instance, you can ask about your recent step count or heart rate readings, find out about activity rings progress, log medications and more.

Recent findings suggest that when asking Siri for health stats, the assistant generates a human natural language response and renders a little inline card that uses familiar user interface elements from the Health app. Similarly, if you ask about your activity rings, a visualisation of your activity rings is shown in the chat transcript.

Sources indicate that again, this is catch-up compared to what you’ve been able to do with old Siri for several years at this point. However, empowered by the LLM behind the scenes, you can ask questions about your health data that are a bit more open-ended.

Sources indicate that you can also do more complicated requests like ‘Send a message to Chance about the status of my activity rings’, or ‘How many steps am I on track to do this week?’. These are the kind of tasks that old Siri would never be able to do.

At least on this current build, the fresh Siri AI Health functionality appears to have been enabled on iOS. It’s currently unclear if the functionality will also be available through watchOS.

iOS 27.3 also introduces a revamped Health app, with a radically newly introduced design that includes new insights, suggestions and views about your health and fitness.

iOS 27.3 is currently in beta and is expected to be released publicly later this year, likely in early December.

Industry observers note that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Wi-Fi Spec: BE5000 (802.11be)Number of Antennas/Removable: 3/NoPorts: One 2.5 Gbps WAN, three 1 Gbps LANProcessor/Memory/Storage: Quad-core 2.0 GHz/1GB/512MBWi-Fi chip: Broadcom BCM6766Peak 802.11ac performance: 1.437 Gbps (at 15 feet)Range: 115 feetSize: 9.8 x 5.9 x 4.0 inchesEstimated Annual Electricity Cost: $13.80.

According to recent reports, as Wi-Fi 7 routers take over as the spec of choice, Netgear reduces the entry point for creating a competent up to date home network to $180 with its Nighthawk RS150. It may not be the fastest, nor does it cover all three Wi-Fi 7 transmission bands but the RS150 provides speedy data service at a budget price. Its dual-band approach to wireless data hits the spec’s hot buttons except for 6 GHz transmissions and the ultra-wide 320MHz data channels that come with it.

At less than $200, is this the best Wi-Fi router or even the best Wi-Fi 7 router for you? Find out in my full review.

With a list price of $200, the Netgear Nighthawk RS150 tempers performance with price. It can be found online for $180. By contrast, the 2025 Editor’s Choice winner, the TP-Link Archer BE3600, is similar in scope at $120.

The lower output BE3600 Nighthawk RS90 can be had for closer to $100 if you’re on a tight budget but still need to upgrade your Wi-Fi.

Looking a lot like the rest of the Nighthawk RS family, the RS150 has an octagonal tower design. At 9.8 x 5.9 x 4.0 inches, it’s three times as big as the TP-Link Archer BE3600, although it takes up only half of its desktop space.

Recent findings suggest that inside, the RS150 has three antennas and a Broadcom BCM6766 for 2x2 data movement for the 2.4 GHz band and 3x3 for the 5.0 GHz band. It relies on many of Wi-Fi 7’s tricks to move more data, including 4K Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM). It does without Multi-Link Operations (MLO) and use of Wi-Fi 7’s 6 GHz band and the associated 320MHz data channels, though.

The router’s quad-core 2.0 GHz processor, 1GB of memory and 512MB create a mid-range home LAN to theoretically move up to 700 Mbps over the 2.4 GHz band as well as 4.3 Gbps on the 5.0 GHz band for a BE5000 rating. It falls short of the best with a 2.5 Gbps WAN input and three 1 Gbps LAN ports versus 5 or 10 Gbps inputs and higher-speed downstream connections.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Industry observers note that most will never miss the fourth networking port but if you need it, the best approach is adding a network switch. It does without the Archer BE3600’s USB port for connecting a data drive too.

According to recent reports, up front, the router’s LEDs show the RS150 status for power, Internet, action on its two bands and three wired connections. There’s also a light for using Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and, happily, a button for turning off the lights.

According to recent reports, unlike many of its Wi-Fi 7 brethren, the RS150 runs cool. Its passive cooling scheme pulls room air into the device with warm air exiting the top vents. Even when running hard, the RS150 never got above 87.2 degrees Fahrenheit compared to 20 degrees hotter for its competitors.

The router includes a 30-day trial for Netgear Armor comprehensive security software that uses Bitdefender software and services. After that, you need to pay. It includes virus scanning for a variety of connected devices along with Dark Web monitoring and heightened analysis of the data flow for malicious sites and unauthorized entry.

The standard proposal costs $100 a year along with an extension of the product’s one year warranty to three years with service and support; without it the personalized service ends at 90 days.

Sources indicate that there’s also the $150 Armor Plus plan that adds Bitdefender’s Virtual Private Network (VPN) in a variety of protocols, including WireGuard and OpenVPN. The subscription also includes anti-tracking and ad blocking.

Based on testing over several weeks of daily use with Keysight’s IxChariot networking benchmark set to mimic 10 high-performance consumers and an HP Envy x360 test notebook, the RS150 started out strong. Able to connect at 1.467 Gbps with the test system next to the RS150, it offers 15% higher throughput compared to the TP-Link Archer BE3600’s 1.234 Gbps.

Industry observers note that later, with a 15 foot length of Cat 7 cable connecting the two, the network provided 1.527 Gbps. That’s a major step up from the Archer BE3600’s 1.103 Gbps.

It did just as well at real-world wireless distances, starting at 15 feet, where the RS150 moved 1.437 Gbps. This is a nice upgrade over the Archer BE3600’s 1.138 Gbps but well short of the Nighthawk RS700 at 1.773 Gbps or the TP-Link Archer BE9700 at 2.201 Gbps, both of which use all three Wi-Fi transmission bands.

It has been revealed that its mid-range figures fluctuated but ended up at an impressive average of 1.057 Gbps at 50 feet. This scatter might feel like extra latency when the router is stressed but the test system never dropped a connection. Still, it’s a large speed boost over the Archer BE9700 (at 700.7 Mbps), Nighthawk RS700 (691.8 Mbps) or Archer BE3600 (702.3 Mbps).

Recent findings suggest that at 75 feet, the throughput fell to 440.8 Mbps, double that of the Archer BE3600, but, again, with lots of variation. The router had a range of 115 feet and delivered 44.7 Mbps at 90 feet – nearly three times the data flow of the Archer BE3600 at the same distance.

It has been revealed that at 1.259 Gbps, the RS150 did well on the wall penetration test where the signal travels across a 20 foot room and then through a wall. That’s just ahead of the Archer BE3600’s 1.114 Gbps.

In a recent development, over three weeks of daily use, the RS150 proved to be an online home body with the ability to move emails, serve up video and serve up online games. Along the way, it used 9.0 watts as it lacks a power-saving idle mode. If it runs 24/7 and you pay the national average of 17.5 cents per kilowatt hour of electricity, the router might cost $13.80 over the year. That’s a couple dollars a year more than the Archer BE3600’s $11.80 annual electricity estimate.

Recent findings suggest that I used the Nighthawk app to get the RS150 online, starting with installing the Nighthawk app on my Samsung Galaxy S25 phone. I snapped the router’s QR code, added my own network name and password and admin credentials. Then I needed to answer two challenge questions and verify my email.

The router connected on the first try and took a little over 11 minutes to set up.

To personalize the RS150, I started with the Nighthawk app updating the system’s firmware.

Later I used the Device Manager to see who was online, the Internet Speed to check my connection and WiFi Analytics to check on the connection’s signal strength. There are settings for changing the Wi-Fi details and using the guest LAN.

The router’s Traffic Meter shows daily, weekly and monthly data use. Unfortunately, the app squeezes this data into a portrait mode page and does not spread it out in landscape orientation.

In a recent development, I also tapped into the router’s interface with a web browser with a functional yet basic page that has a scrolling ticker for the network names and passwords. In other words, don’t let just anyone see it.

The Advanced pages range from running the hardware as an access point to turning off the LED lights.

It has been revealed that as Wi-Fi 7 matures and the gear to enable it comes down in price, Netgear’s Nighthawk RS150 hits a sweet spot with a nice price and superior performance compared to other budget routers. It excels at mid-range distances and range where competitors can’t keep up.

Recent findings suggest that sure, there’re compromises, like the lack of 6GHz data transmissions, presence of only three downstream wired networking ports and having to pay for personalized support for more than three months. That mentioned, those items pale in comparison to the RS150’s ability to move data around the house and at a peak of over 1.4 Gbps and stay online at 115 feet.

In other words, the Nighthawk RS150 should satisfy most home networkers with performance that’s hard to beat at $180.

The Cannes Film Festival has issued a statement protesting recent legal sanctions against Iranian Palme d’Or-winning director Jafar Panahi, including a five-year, one-month prison sentence and travel ban.

The statement comes just three weeks after news broke that Panahi is caught once again in the crosshairs of the Iranian authorities.

It has been revealed that “The Festival de Cannes strongly condemns the judicial persecution of Jafar Panahi and calls for the lifting of all restrictions that prevent him from traveling, creating, and expressing himself freely,” noted the festival. Related Stories News Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 News Jafar Panahi Back In Crosshairs Of Iranian Authorities With Five-Year Sentence.

Recent findings suggest that “Like artists, festivals, and cultural institutions around the world, the Festival de Cannes calls on the international community to take action and speak with one voice to prevent his imprisonment. His freedom is not just about one filmmaker, it is about the rights of all artists to think, create, and express themselves without fear of imprisonment,” it continued. Watch on Deadline.

“Everyone knows this, and everyone stands up for it: ‘No artist should be imprisoned for their work, their ideas or their expression, in Iran or anywhere.’.

Local media reported in mid-October that Panahi, who spent much of 2025 and early 2026 outside of Iran on the awards trail with Cannes Palme d’Or winner It Was Just Sent An Accident, has been given a five-year, one-month prison sentence.

His lawyer Mostafa Nili told local media that Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court had slapped Panahi with a five-year sentence, two-year social media and travel ban, and also issued an order for the confiscation of Panahi’s possessions and assets.

Nili and his client paid a visit to the Sentence Enforcement Unit of the Culture and Media Prosecutor’s Office, where they learned that Panahi had been convicted “in absentia” in a separate case.

The director at the moment has three open cases in Iran but according to Nili had not been officially summoned for hearings, even though he is in the country.

Panahi returned home immediately after the March 15 ceremony for the 2026 Academy Awards in which It Was Just An Accident was nominated and has not left since.

The upcoming sentence comes on top of a separate one-year prison sentence and a two-year travel meted out by the Iranian Branch 26 court in 2025, on charges of “propaganda activities against the system.”.

Industry observers note that panahi has long been in the crosshairs of Iran’s hardline Islamic Republic authorities. He spent seven months in the country’s notoriously tough Evin jail after being arrested in July 2022. Iranian authorities reactivated a six-year sentence originally given to Panahi in 2010 alongside a 20-year filmmaking and travel ban.

He had originally gone to the prison to enquire about the whereabouts of fellow filmmakers Mohammad Rasoulof and Mostafa Al-Ahmad who had been arrested a few days previously for criticizing the actions of the authorities in an open letter.

According to recent reports, the reactivated sentence was connected to Panahi’s attendance of a funeral in 2009 of a student shot dead in the Green Revolution and his later attempt to shoot a feature set against the backdrop of the uprising. He was released in February 2023 after going on hunger strike.

It seemed for a time that the authorities were softening their stance towards the director after he was granted permission to travel to Cannes for the first time in 15 years in 2025 for the premiere of clandestinely shot film It Was Just An Accident. It went on to win the Palme d’Or and then be Oscar nominated in the Best International Feature Film Category as the French entry.

While on the final stages of awards campaign trail, Panahi publicly denounced a deadly crackdown on pro-democracy protests which swept Iran in January 2026 in which tens of thousands are believe to have died.

In spite of the tense political situation in Iran and potential threat to his own freedom, Panahi vowed to return home as soon as his Oscar contender duties were done and dusted, which he did.

The director has a long relationship with the Cannes Film Festival ever since his first film The White Balloon won the Caméra d’Or in 1995.

A number of his films have played in the festival including Panahi’s films on numerous occasions, including Crimson G ol d , which won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize in 2003, and 3 F aces, which was presented in Competition in 2018 and won the Best Screenplay Award.

In 2010, he was invited to serve on the jurywhile he was imprisoned in Iran. His seat remained empty during the opening ceremony.

It has been revealed that “Fifteen years later, in 2025, Jafar Panahi took the stage to receive the Palme d’Or for I t W a s J ust an A cci d ent. This award honored a career dedicated to defending creative freedom and freedom of expression,” wrote the festival.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The one thing Apple’s own MagSafe wallet does that a few third-party wallets have is Find My. If you misplace your wallet, your iPhone tells you where it is. Most MagSafe wallets either skip tracking entirely or have a pocket for an AirTag, which adds thickness and it’s another thing to buy. The MOFT Trackable Field Wallet builds the tracker into the wallet itself, so it reveals up in the Find My app.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

MOFT has been making the origami-style folding wallet for many years, and this model works like any other Find My accessory. So that means you get left-behind alerts when you leave without it, and the ability to make it trackable through Apple’s network if it’s across town instead of under the couch. It also works with Google’s Find Hub on Android, which matters if you’ve got a mixed household of devices.

The wallet is powered by a built-in battery rather than a watch-style battery, and MOFT says a charge lasts about six months. You charge it by placing the wallet on a Qi charger for about an hour and a half, which, in practice, means dropping it on a MagSafe dock twice a year. That’s a better setup than an AirTag in a wallet as well.

Recent findings suggest that the wallet holds up to eight cards, or closer to four to six if you also use the hidden compartment for cash. A pull tab in the wallet brings your everyday cards out in one motion, while your driver’s license and cash stay tucked inside of it. It’s made from MOFT’s vegan leather and at 14 mm thick, it’s slimmer than a traditional wallet but noticeably thicker than Apple’s card-only wallet, which is the price you are going to pay to hold up this much stuff.

It has been revealed that the stand is the usual MOFT origami fold-out, and it works in portrait and landscape for FaceTime or watching a video on the plane. You can buy it without the stand if you’d rather have the thinner version. It comes in Jet Black, Misty Cove, Terracotta, and Peony.

Recent findings suggest that two things to know going in. There’s no RFID blocking in this version (MOFT has a non-Find My Snap Field Wallet if you want that). MOFT also warns that the magnets can affect magnetic-stripe cards, so avoid putting a hotel key in it.

I’ve spent the past month on a Pelican accessory beat, using wallets designed for outdoor use. The MOFT Trackable Field Wallet is the other end of that accessory spectrum: more cards, a stand, and Find My built in. If Find My is the reason you’ve stuck with Apple’s wallet, this is a really nice option that holds a bunch and is trackable.

The MOFT Trackable Field Wallet is available on Amazon and directly from MOFT.

Tech Report: Nimony: A New Compiler for Nim

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (438 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nimony

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unpack, put bin/ on your PATH, done — and with nimony n you do not even need a C compiler.
  • Sources indicate that nimony is a new compiler for Nim and the home of the Nim 3 language: borrow checking, explicit nilability, sum types, checked generics and more, with incremental and parallel builds from the start.
  • Variant objects no longer need a separate discriminator enum: tags live in the case section, and `case value of Tag(fields):` pattern matching binds the fields for that arm — like expressions you’d write in ML-family languages, checked for exhaustiveness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Built every day from nimony’s master branch.

Unpack, put bin/ on your PATH, done — and with nimony n you do not even need a C compiler. Download page · Build from source · Tools.

Sources indicate that nimony is a new compiler for Nim and the home of the Nim 3 language: borrow checking, explicit nilability, sum types, checked generics and more, with incremental and parallel builds from the start. For how it relates to Nim 2, see the FAQ.

Here is a taste of the language.

Variant objects no longer need a separate discriminator enum: tags live in the case section, and `case value of Tag(fields):` pattern matching binds the fields for that arm — like expressions you’d write in ML-family languages, checked for exhaustiveness.

type Expr = ref object case of Lit: value: int of Add, Sub: left, right: Expr proc eval(e: Expr): int = case e of Lit(value): result = value of Add(left, right): result = eval(left) + eval(right) of Sub(left, right): result = eval(left) - eval(right) echo eval(Add(left: Lit(value: 10), right: Lit(value: 32))) # 42.

Shared fields can live outside the case, variants can nest (seq[Tree] in a branch), and grouped matchers like {Add, Sub}(left, right) appear where multiple tags share the same shape — see Case in object in the manual.

Nimony rejects classic footguns at compile time:.

proc grow(s: var seq[int]; use: int) = s.add use var s = @[1, 2, 3] # for v in s: # grow(s, v) # Error: `s` is borrowed during iteration — no realloc under active borrows.

This follows prefix exclusion: while s (or s.elements) is borrowed, that path cannot be mutated until the borrow ends — sibling fields can still be updated.

In a recent development, by default generics are type checked: the code is checked when the generic is defined, not only when it is instantiated! Duck typing is still available, you get it via the {.untyped.} pragma.

The required operations are described via concepts:.

type Comparable = concept proc `<`(a, b: Self): bool proc min[T: Comparable](a, b: T): T = if a < b: a else: b echo min(3, 7) echo min("b", "a").

Sources indicate that container-style concepts (e.g. Findable[T]) work the same way with iterators and indexed access — see Concepts and Generics in the manual.

Industry observers note that 2026-09-08 Nimony 0.6.2 has been released. It ships with a guest report from a user who spent a year porting real projects over. A Vulkan visualiser, a web framework, an embedded server: Nim, one year in.

Older entries, including the 0.2 release, live on the News page.

Google buys superhot geothermal power from Quaise for Oregon data centres

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quaise Energy’s Project Obsidian site in central Oregon.
  • Google will buy 50 megawatts of “superhot” geothermal power from Quaise Energy’s Project Obsidian in central Oregon.
  • In a recent development, the deal is worth more than $500m, Benoît Morenne reported for the Wall Street Journal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quaise Energy’s Project Obsidian site in central Oregon.

Google will buy 50 megawatts of “superhot” geothermal power from Quaise Energy’s Project Obsidian in central Oregon. Deliveries start as early as 2030. The electricity will support Google’s existing data centres in The Dalles, Oregon, Quaise declared on Tuesday.

In a recent development, the deal is worth more than $500m, Benoît Morenne reported for the Wall Street Journal. Quaise told the newspaper the project will cost about $350m.

It has been revealed that “It is Google basically putting their thumb on the scale and saying, ‘Okay, we like this. We like what this looks like,’” Quaise CEO Carlos Araque told the WSJ.

It has been revealed that conventional geothermal plants tap natural hot-water reservoirs that rarely pass 200°C (400°F), Quaise noted. Its plant aims for far hotter rock. That rock can produce up to 10 times more power per well, the company claims.

Quaise will first drill to about 4km with conventional tools, the WSJ reported. It will then switch to a gyrotron, which fires millimetre waves that vaporise rock. That takes the well to about 4.8km. Water pumped into the wells will heat up, and the steam will drive the turbines.

Sources indicate that quaise notes Obsidian will be the first plant to make electricity from rock above 300°C. It has not yet proven the technology at commercial scale, the WSJ noted.

Quaise expects 200 to 400 construction jobs and more than 50 permanent ones at the site. It raised $134m in July and closed its Series B at $180m in August, including $35m from Nabors Industries. In September, the US Department of Energy picked Obsidian for up to $25m in support, Quaise’s press releases show.

Google is looking for electricity to run upcoming data centres and AI. In September, it signed a 396MW geothermal deal with Fervo Energy. It also works with companies building nuclear power and long-duration storage, the WSJ reported.

Lucia Tian, who leads Google’s advanced energy work, told the WSJ that the scale of power Google needs requires it to “foster that ecosystem”.

Google says it pays for all the power its data centres use. It also covers the grid upgrades its growth requires, and its three Oregon campuses run on 83% carbon-free energy.

Earlier this month, US voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures. Google’s first Wyoming data centre, announced earlier this month, will run on gas with carbon capture.

Klarna tops $1bn in revenue for a fourth quarter, still loses $65m

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, klarna grew revenue 12% to $1.009bn in the third quarter of 2026, its fourth quarter in a row above $1bn.
  • Recent findings suggest that it still made a net loss of $65m, compared with a $95m loss in the same quarter of 2025.
  • “Q3 was our fourth straight quarter with revenue above 1 billion dollars and positive adjusted operating income.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, klarna grew revenue 12% to $1.009bn in the third quarter of 2026, its fourth quarter in a row above $1bn. Adjusted operating income reached $21m, up from a $14m loss a year ago, the Swedish payments tech giant remarked on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that it still made a net loss of $65m, compared with a $95m loss in the same quarter of 2025. The operating loss was $53m. Klarna put this down to share-based payments, which rose 38% to $54m in its annual pay cycle, according to its earnings release.

“Q3 was our fourth straight quarter with revenue above 1 billion dollars and positive adjusted operating income. We are keeping more of each dollar we process through our everyday finance network,” CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski said.

Shoppers spent $36.1bn through Klarna in the quarter, up 10%. In the US, spending rose 24% to $8.2bn, and the US now makes up 23% of the total.

In a recent development, most of that US growth came from Fair Financing, Klarna’s longer-term loans for bigger purchases. Globally, Fair Financing grew 61% to $5.2bn. Pay Later, its interest-free split payments, still accounts for about three quarters of volume.

Klarna now has 122 million active people and 1.35 million merchants, up 59%. Klarna credits payment processors that switch it on by default, such as Fiserv’s Clover, which went live at 100,000 US stores in October. The Klarna Card more than doubled to $4.5bn in volume, and subscription revenue rose more than 500% to $43m.

Sources indicate that klarna also mentioned Apple Upgrade is gaining traction. Apple debuted the Klarna-backed device leasing programme in July.

It has been revealed that transaction margin, the revenue left after processing, credit and funding costs, rose 32% to $371m. Provisions for bad loans fell to 0.56% of volume, from 0.72%. Customer deposits of $12.7bn made up 88% of its funding. In June, it debuted US savings accounts.

According to recent reports, some credit measures moved the other way. In the US, Fair Financing loans more than 30 days overdue rose to 3.7%, from 3.5% a year ago. Klarna said it expected the rise, which reflects financing on the Klarna Card. Adjusted general and administrative costs rose 43%.

Klarna kept its full-year outlook: $4.08bn to $4.16bn in revenue, and $280m to $300m in adjusted operating income. It expects a net profit in the fourth quarter.

Industry observers note that klarna has also changed its leadership this month. On 12 November, it named Chris Koegel of Robinhood as chief financial officer from January, replacing Niclas Neglén. On Monday, it hired Brandon Gracey from Shopify to run North America.

Klarna listed in New York at $40 a share. By April, its shares were 76% below their high. In July, it applied for a US banking licence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock.

Recent findings suggest that this is exactly the kind of attack Report URI is designed to detect. Our platform can identify unexpected changes to trusted JavaScript, detect upcoming scripts being loaded and reveal suspicious connections to external destinations. In this case, those signals would have exposed the malicious activity, even though the original script was being served from a trusted Optimizely domain. With an appropriate CSP in enforcement mode, organisations could have gone a step further and blocked key parts of the attack before they succeeded.

The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn't always remain trustworthy. A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.

According to recent reports, most of the malicious code has now been removed. At 21:52 UTC we found it in only 1 of the 188 infected snippets, down from 169 at 20:56 UTC. If your site uses Optimizely Web, or you visited any of the sites below today, read on.

Recent findings suggest that optimizely Web works by having each customer load a JavaScript "snippet" from Optimizely's CDN, for example https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js. The snippet contains Optimizely's code, the customer's experiments and an optional field called Project JavaScript (projectJS): custom code the customer writes in their Optimizely dashboard, which runs on every page.

The attacker wrote their own code into the Project JavaScript of customer projects, and the rest of each snippet was untouched. The file was still served from cdn.optimizely.com, with Optimizely's certificate, from a host that every affected site already trusted. Here is what was added to Zoom's snippet:.

We saw three versions of the injected loader:.
